patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Collections Requirement 1, what practices protect a physical collection (such as stamps, postcards, patches, or historical ephemera) from long-term deterioration while maintaining its provenance?
options: A. Catalog each item with its origin, date, and condition grade, and store items in archival acid-free, lignin-free, and PVC-free holders away from direct ultraviolet sunlight, high heat, and damp basements or attics.
B. Laminate historical paper items in irreversible hot plastic pouches and display them in a south-facing window to keep them warm.
C. Fasten collectible patches and paper documents to corrugated cardboard using rubber cement and store them in an uninsulated garage.
D. Discard all original boxes, certificates, and acquisition notes so the items take up less shelf space.
choices: A. Catalog each item with its origin, date, and condition grade, and store items in archival acid-free, lignin-free, and PVC-free holders away from direct ultraviolet sunlight, high heat, and damp basements or attics.
B. Laminate historical paper items in irreversible hot plastic pouches and display them in a south-facing window to keep them warm.
C. Fasten collectible patches and paper documents to corrugated cardboard using rubber cement and store them in an uninsulated garage.
D. Discard all original boxes, certificates, and acquisition notes so the items take up less shelf space.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Catalog each item with its origin, date, and condition grade, and store items in archival acid-free, lignin-free, and PVC-free holders away from direct ultraviolet sunlight, high heat, and damp basements or attics.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Proper collection care combines detailed cataloging (provenance, description, and condition) with archival, acid-free storage in a stable, low-humidity environment shielded from UV light.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How did the Industrial Revolution in the early 1800s transform the hobby of collecting?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How did the Industrial Revolution in the early 1800s transform the hobby of collecting?
options: A. It outlawed private ownership of ancient coins and rare books
B. Mass production allowed a broader consumer society to afford and collect all kinds of manufactured goods
C. It replaced glass and clay marbles entirely with hand-carved marble statues
D. It restricted collecting to government museums and university archives
choices: A. It outlawed private ownership of ancient coins and rare books
B. Mass production allowed a broader consumer society to afford and collect all kinds of manufactured goods
C. It replaced glass and clay marbles entirely with hand-carved marble statues
D. It restricted collecting to government museums and university archives
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Mass production allowed a broader consumer society to afford and collect all kinds of manufactured goods
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Before the early 1800s, mainly wealthy people collected fine art and rare books, but mass production during the Industrial Revolution made affordable goods available to everyday collectors (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the main reasons cited in the pamphlet for maintaining a master catalog of your collection?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the main reasons cited in the pamphlet for maintaining a master catalog of your collection?
options: A. Proving the genuineness and history of the items in your collection
B. Keeping a record of financial transactions for tax reporting if you sell for a large profit
C. Providing documentation if your collection becomes valuable enough to require insurance
D. Guaranteeing that every item in the binder will automatically double in price each year
choices: A. Proving the genuineness and history of the items in your collection
B. Keeping a record of financial transactions for tax reporting if you sell for a large profit
C. Providing documentation if your collection becomes valuable enough to require insurance
D. Guaranteeing that every item in the binder will automatically double in price each year
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Guaranteeing that every item in the binder will automatically double in price each year
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Proper cataloging helps prove genuineness, records financial transactions for tax purposes, and supports insurance documentation, but it does not guarantee price appreciation (p. 11).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is it difficult to look up the exact monetary value of a nonprecious rock or mineral collection in a book?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is it difficult to look up the exact monetary value of a nonprecious rock or mineral collection in a book?
options: A. Federal law prohibits publishing prices for geological specimens
B. Common rocks are only traded by weight in metric tons between mining companies
C. Standard price guides do not exist for nonprecious rocks as they do for coins or cards, so collectors compare prices at rock shows and shops
D. Every rock specimen loses all monetary value the moment it is removed from the ground
choices: A. Federal law prohibits publishing prices for geological specimens
B. Common rocks are only traded by weight in metric tons between mining companies
C. Standard price guides do not exist for nonprecious rocks as they do for coins or cards, so collectors compare prices at rock shows and shops
D. Every rock specimen loses all monetary value the moment it is removed from the ground
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Standard price guides do not exist for nonprecious rocks as they do for coins or cards, so collectors compare prices at rock shows and shops
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Because there are no standard price guides for nonprecious rocks and minerals, collectors visit rock shops and mineral shows to see what sellers charge for comparable specimens (p. 15).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What rule must rock collectors follow regarding state parks, national parks, and private property?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What rule must rock collectors follow regarding state parks, national parks, and private property?
options: A. You may collect up to five pounds of rocks per day inside any national park
B. Collecting in state and national parks or monuments is illegal, and you must get permission before collecting on private property
C. Private property is open to rock hunting without permission as long as you do not use power tools
D. Only fossils are protected in national monuments, while minerals and gemstones are free to take
choices: A. You may collect up to five pounds of rocks per day inside any national park
B. Collecting in state and national parks or monuments is illegal, and you must get permission before collecting on private property
C. Private property is open to rock hunting without permission as long as you do not use power tools
D. Only fossils are protected in national monuments, while minerals and gemstones are free to take
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Collecting in state and national parks or monuments is illegal, and you must get permission before collecting on private property
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Collecting rocks in state parks, national parks, or national monuments is illegal, and collectors must always obtain permission from the landowner or land manager on private land (p. 35).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why did the 1909 Honus Wagner baseball card become one of the scarcest and most famous sports cards in history?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why did the 1909 Honus Wagner baseball card become one of the scarcest and most famous sports cards in history?
options: A. A warehouse fire destroyed all but one printing plate at the card factory
B. Wagner demanded his picture be removed from the tobacco-sponsored card set, either to discourage children from using tobacco or over a pay dispute
C. The card was printed on experimental gold foil for only one week
D. Major League Baseball banned all Pittsburgh Pirates players from appearing on cards in 1909
choices: A. A warehouse fire destroyed all but one printing plate at the card factory
B. Wagner demanded his picture be removed from the tobacco-sponsored card set, either to discourage children from using tobacco or over a pay dispute
C. The card was printed on experimental gold foil for only one week
D. Major League Baseball banned all Pittsburgh Pirates players from appearing on cards in 1909
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Wagner demanded his picture be removed from the tobacco-sponsored card set, either to discourage children from using tobacco or over a pay dispute
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In 1909, Pittsburgh Pirates shortstop Honus Wagner objected to his image appearing on a tobacco card, either to keep from encouraging children to use tobacco or because he wanted a share of the profits, halting production (p. 49).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do professional positions at museums, galleries, and auction houses usually require formal education and specialized training beyond hobbyist experience?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do professional positions at museums, galleries, and auction houses usually require formal education and specialized training beyond hobbyist experience?
options: A. Because employees must manufacture new replicas of every antique in the building
B. Because high financial, historical, and preservation stakes require verified expertise in areas like appraisal, curation, or conservation
C. Because federal law requires a medical degree to handle porcelain or paintings
D. Because museum staff are prohibited from having any personal interest in collecting
choices: A. Because employees must manufacture new replicas of every antique in the building
B. Because high financial, historical, and preservation stakes require verified expertise in areas like appraisal, curation, or conservation
C. Because federal law requires a medical degree to handle porcelain or paintings
D. Because museum staff are prohibited from having any personal interest in collecting
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Because high financial, historical, and preservation stakes require verified expertise in areas like appraisal, curation, or conservation
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Although a collector's focused knowledge is a helpful start, formal schooling and training are often necessary for appraisers, curators, and conservators because so much financial and historical value is at stake (p. 60).

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) For one day, keep a log in which you describe your communication activities. Keep track of the time and different ways you spend communicating, such as talking person-to-person, listening to teachers, listening to the radio or podcasts, watching television, using social media, reading books and other print media, and using any electronic communication device. Discuss with your counselor what your log reveals about the importance of communication in your life. Think of ways to improve your communication skills. (b) For three days, keep a journal of your listening experiences. Identify one example of each of the following, and discuss with your counselor when you have listened to each: obtain information, be persuaded, appreciate or enjoy something, and understand someone's feelings. (c) In a small-group setting, meet with other Scouts or with friends. Have them share personal stories about significant events in their lives that affected them in some way. Take note of how each Scout participates in the group discussion and how effectively each Scout communicates their story. Report what you have learned to your counselor about the differences you observed in effective communication. (d) List as many ways as you can think of to communicate with others (face-to-face, by telephone, letter, email, text messages, social media, and so on). For each type of communication, discuss with your counselor an instance when that method might not be appropriate or effective.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: During an interpersonal conversation or troop leadership council meeting for Communication Requirement 1, which behavior demonstrates effective active listening?
quiz_item.question: During an interpersonal conversation or troop leadership council meeting for Communication Requirement 1, which behavior demonstrates effective active listening?
options: A. Interrupting the speaker mid-sentence to offer your own story while checking text messages on your phone.
B. Crossing your arms, looking at the floor, and formulating a rebuttal before the other person finishes speaking.
C. Repeating the exact same loud slogan louder each time an audience member asks a clarifying question.

D. Maintaining appropriate eye contact and open posture, avoiding distractions, waiting until the speaker finishes, and paraphrasing or asking clarifying questions to confirm you understood their message.
choices: A. Interrupting the speaker mid-sentence to offer your own story while checking text messages on your phone.
B. Crossing your arms, looking at the floor, and formulating a rebuttal before the other person finishes speaking.
C. Repeating the exact same loud slogan louder each time an audience member asks a clarifying question.

D. Maintaining appropriate eye contact and open posture, avoiding distractions, waiting until the speaker finishes, and paraphrasing or asking clarifying questions to confirm you understood their message.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Maintaining appropriate eye contact and open posture, avoiding distractions, waiting until the speaker finishes, and paraphrasing or asking clarifying questions to confirm you understood their message.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Active listening involves attentiveness to both verbal content and nonverbal cues, withholding premature judgment, and paraphrasing key points to verify accurate understanding.

pamphlet_excerpts: Checking Availability by Phone: If you contact the person by phone, ask if this is a good time to talk (p. 33).
Scheduling a Callback Time: If it is not a good time, ask when you should call back (p. 33).
Verifying Names and Titles: Start by asking the person to spell his or her name and tell you his or her title (p. 33).
Speaking Clearly and Rephrasing: Speak clearly and slowly so the person can understand your questions. If you do not understand a response, ask the same question in another way (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Confirm Spelling and Titles: Start by asking the person to spell his or her name and tell you his or her title (p. 33).
Step 2 - Ask Clear Research Questions: Speak clearly and slowly so the person can understand your questions. If you do not understand a response, ask the same question in another way (p. 33).
Step 3 - Paraphrase to Verify Accuracy: You could also state the response in your ownwords and ask if you got it right (p. 33).
Step 4 - Save Tough Questions for Last: Use follow-up questions todig more deeply into a topic. Save your hardest questions for last (p. 33).

pamphlet_excerpts: Selecting a Local Subject: Tips for Interviewing and Introducing a Guest Speaker Let's say you have a neighbor who is a police detective (p. 17).
Extending a Speaker Invitation: You also need to show your counselor how you will invite your neighbor to speak at the meeting (p. 17).
Preparing Note-Taking Tools: Have as mall notebook and pen or a laptop or computer with you when you make the call (p. 17).
Using Hands-Free Headsets: If you have a wireless headset for a cell phone, you can listen hands-free while typing your notes (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Gather Notebook or Laptop: Have as mall notebook and pen or a laptop or computer with you when you make the call (p. 17).
Step 2 - Set Up Hands-Free Audio: If you have a wireless headset for a cell phone, you can listen hands-free while typing your notes (p. 17).
Step 3 - Make a Polite Request: Tell the neighbor that you are a member of Scouts BSA and ask her politely if you could interview her as part of your Communication merit (p. 17).
Step 4 - Explain the Interview Purpose: Explain that the requirements include interviewing and preparing to introduce a guest speaker (p. 17).

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Write to the editor of a magazine or your local newspaper to express your opinion or share information on any subject you choose. Send your message by fax, email, or regular mail. (b) Create a webpage or blog of special interest to you (for instance, your troop or crew, a hobby, or a sport). Include at least three articles or entries and one photograph or illustration, and one link to some other webpage or blog that would be helpful to someone who visits the webpage or blog you have created. Note: It is not necessary to post your webpage or blog to the internet, but if you decide to do so, you must first share it with your parent or guardian and counselor and get their permission. (c) Use desktop publishing to produce a newsletter, brochure, flyer, or other printed material for your troop or crew, class at school, or other group. Include at least one article and one photograph or illustration.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During an interpersonal conversation or troop leadership council meeting for Communication Requirement 1, which behavior demonstrates effective active listening?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: During an interpersonal conversation or troop leadership council meeting for Communication Requirement 1, which behavior demonstrates effective active listening?
options: A. Interrupting the speaker mid-sentence to offer your own story while checking text messages on your phone.
B. Crossing your arms, looking at the floor, and formulating a rebuttal before the other person finishes speaking.
C. Repeating the exact same loud slogan louder each time an audience member asks a clarifying question.

D. Maintaining appropriate eye contact and open posture, avoiding distractions, waiting until the speaker finishes, and paraphrasing or asking clarifying questions to confirm you understood their message.
choices: A. Interrupting the speaker mid-sentence to offer your own story while checking text messages on your phone.
B. Crossing your arms, looking at the floor, and formulating a rebuttal before the other person finishes speaking.
C. Repeating the exact same loud slogan louder each time an audience member asks a clarifying question.

D. Maintaining appropriate eye contact and open posture, avoiding distractions, waiting until the speaker finishes, and paraphrasing or asking clarifying questions to confirm you understood their message.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Maintaining appropriate eye contact and open posture, avoiding distractions, waiting until the speaker finishes, and paraphrasing or asking clarifying questions to confirm you understood their message.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Active listening involves attentiveness to both verbal content and nonverbal cues, withholding premature judgment, and paraphrasing key points to verify accurate understanding.

D. Avoid mentioning any specific benefits until the listener asks a question

D. Right at the beginning before asking if it is a good time to talk
choices: A. At the very end of the conversation after building rapport

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): After verifying basic details and using follow-up questions to explore the topic, you should save your hardest questions for last (p. 33).

choices: A. Put the phone in another room and type from memory after the call ends

options: A. Including only the arguments made by the loudest speaker in the room
B. Accurately summarizing all points of view expressed on the issue without bias
C. Leaving out any viewpoint that disagrees with your personal opinion
D. Rewriting the speakers' quotes to make one side sound foolish
choices: A. Including only the arguments made by the loudest speaker in the room

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Before mixing two-part epoxy or polyester resin with fiberglass or carbon fiber reinforcement for Composite Materials Requirement 1, what safety precautions are mandatory?
quiz_item.question: Before mixing two-part epoxy or polyester resin with fiberglass or carbon fiber reinforcement for Composite Materials Requirement 1, what safety precautions are mandatory?
options: A. Mix large batches of resin and catalyst in a tall, narrow plastic cup inside an unventilated closet and handle cut glass fibers with bare hands.

B. Read the Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all resins and hardeners, work in a well-ventilated area, wear chemical-resistant nitrile gloves, safety goggles, long sleeves, and an appropriate dust mask/respirator, and mix small batches in shallow containers to prevent runaway exothermic heat.
C. Heat the hardener catalyst over an open flame to speed up curing and blow fiberglass sanding dust across the room with compressed air.
D. Wash uncured epoxy resin off bare skin using acetone or lacquer thinner so the solvent carries the chemicals deeper into your pores.

quiz_item.question: What is the fundamental difference between thermoset resins and thermoplastic resins?
options: A. Thermoset resins harden irreversibly through crosslinking, while thermoplastics can be remelted and recycled
B. Thermoplastics permanently crosslink and can never be softened by heat
C. Thermoset resins are only used in children's toys and disposable food containers
D. Thermoplastic resins require fiberglass to become solid at room temperature
choices: A. Thermoset resins harden irreversibly through crosslinking, while thermoplastics can be remelted and recycled

C. Thermoset resins are only used in children's toys and disposable food containers

quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Thermoset resins harden irreversibly through crosslinking, while thermoplastics can be remelted and recycled
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Thermoset resins change from liquid to solid in an irreversible crosslinking reaction, whereas thermoplastic hardening is reversible so the material can be remelted and recycled (p. 31).

Overlapping Fiberglass Seams Properly: When you join pieces of fiberglass reinforcement to form a seam, overlap the pieces by 1 to 3 inches (p. 60).
Preserving Structural Laminate Strength: This ensures that the structural properties of the laminate are not weakened (p. 60).
Staggering Multi-Layer Overlaps: If you use more than one layer of reinforcement, be sure to stagger or space out the overlaps to avoid thick buildups that also can create weak areas (p. 60).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Maintain Seam Overlap Strength: This ensures that the structural properties of the laminate are not weakened (p. 60).

Step 2 - Stagger Multi-Layer Seam Overlaps: If you use more than one layer of reinforcement, be sure to stagger or space out the overlaps to avoid thick buildups that also can create weak areas (p. 60).
Step 3 - Eliminate Trapped Air Pockets: When you saturate the fiberglass reinforcement with resin, air can be trapped in the laminate, creating voids (p. 60).
Step 4 - Inspect Cured Laminate for Voids: Air voids are simply bubbles, which when trapped in the cured laminate can cause problems ranging from poor appearance to structural failure (p. 60).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before mixing two-part epoxy or polyester resin with fiberglass or carbon fiber reinforcement for Composite Materials Requirement 1, what safety precautions are mandatory?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before mixing two-part epoxy or polyester resin with fiberglass or carbon fiber reinforcement for Composite Materials Requirement 1, what safety precautions are mandatory?
options: A. Mix large batches of resin and catalyst in a tall, narrow plastic cup inside an unventilated closet and handle cut glass fibers with bare hands.

B. Read the Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all resins and hardeners, work in a well-ventilated area, wear chemical-resistant nitrile gloves, safety goggles, long sleeves, and an appropriate dust mask/respirator, and mix small batches in shallow containers to prevent runaway exothermic heat.
C. Heat the hardener catalyst over an open flame to speed up curing and blow fiberglass sanding dust across the room with compressed air.
D. Wash uncured epoxy resin off bare skin using acetone or lacquer thinner so the solvent carries the chemicals deeper into your pores.
choices: A. Mix large batches of resin and catalyst in a tall, narrow plastic cup inside an unventilated closet and handle cut glass fibers with bare hands.

B. Read the Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all resins and hardeners, work in a well-ventilated area, wear chemical-resistant nitrile gloves, safety goggles, long sleeves, and an appropriate dust mask/respirator, and mix small batches in shallow containers to prevent runaway exothermic heat.
C. Heat the hardener catalyst over an open flame to speed up curing and blow fiberglass sanding dust across the room with compressed air.
D. Wash uncured epoxy resin off bare skin using acetone or lacquer thinner so the solvent carries the chemicals deeper into your pores.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Read the Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all resins and hardeners, work in a well-ventilated area, wear chemical-resistant nitrile gloves, safety goggles, long sleeves, and an appropriate dust mask/respirator, and mix small batches in shallow containers to prevent runaway exothermic heat.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Composite fibers cause skin and respiratory irritation and curing resins generate exothermic heat and fumes; SDS review, ventilation, gloves, eye protection, respiratory protection, and shallow mixing cups prevent chemical burns and overheating.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How did the use of modern composite materials change during and immediately after World War II?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How did the use of modern composite materials change during and immediately after World War II?
options: A. Composites were abandoned in favor of solid copper and cast iron
B. Military use in aircraft and watercraft led to rapid postwar growth in boats, cars, tanks, and pipes
C. Composites were restricted exclusively to residential brickmaking
D. The Navy banned composites because they corroded faster than steel in saltwater
choices: A. Composites were abandoned in favor of solid copper and cast iron
B. Military use in aircraft and watercraft led to rapid postwar growth in boats, cars, tanks, and pipes
C. Composites were restricted exclusively to residential brickmaking
D. The Navy banned composites because they corroded faster than steel in saltwater
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Military use in aircraft and watercraft led to rapid postwar growth in boats, cars, tanks, and pipes
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): After the U.S. Air Force and Navy proved the value of composites in wartime aircraft and watercraft, commercial applications grew rapidly for boats, trucks, sports cars, tanks, and pipes (p. 19).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the fundamental difference between thermoset resins and thermoplastic resins?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the fundamental difference between thermoset resins and thermoplastic resins?
options: A. Thermoset resins harden irreversibly through crosslinking, while thermoplastics can be remelted and recycled
B. Thermoplastics permanently crosslink and can never be softened by heat
C. Thermoset resins are only used in children's toys and disposable food containers
D. Thermoplastic resins require fiberglass to become solid at room temperature
choices: A. Thermoset resins harden irreversibly through crosslinking, while thermoplastics can be remelted and recycled
B. Thermoplastics permanently crosslink and can never be softened by heat
C. Thermoset resins are only used in children's toys and disposable food containers
D. Thermoplastic resins require fiberglass to become solid at room temperature
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Thermoset resins harden irreversibly through crosslinking, while thermoplastics can be remelted and recycled
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Thermoset resins change from liquid to solid in an irreversible crosslinking reaction, whereas thermoplastic hardening is reversible so the material can be remelted and recycled (p. 31).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do composite manufacturers often incorporate balsa wood, foam, or honeycomb into a laminate?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do composite manufacturers often incorporate balsa wood, foam, or honeycomb into a laminate?
options: A. They dissolve completely when exposed to thermoset resin
B. They replace the need for any mold or clamping hardware
C. They serve as the glossy outer gelcoat finish on boats
D. They act as lightweight core materials that increase stiffness and thickness without heavy solid resin buildup
choices: A. They dissolve completely when exposed to thermoset resin
B. They replace the need for any mold or clamping hardware
C. They serve as the glossy outer gelcoat finish on boats
D. They act as lightweight core materials that increase stiffness and thickness without heavy solid resin buildup
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. They act as lightweight core materials that increase stiffness and thickness without heavy solid resin buildup
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Balsa, foam varieties, and honeycomb serve as lightweight core materials sandwiched between reinforcement layers to add rigidity without excessive weight (p. 40).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How should you join pieces of fiberglass reinforcement across multiple layers in a composite project?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How should you join pieces of fiberglass reinforcement across multiple layers in a composite project?
options: A. Leave a half-inch gap between fabric edges so pure resin fills the seam
B. Overlap seams by 1 to 3 inches and stagger the overlaps between layers
C. Stack all overlaps directly on top of one another to create a thick ridge
D. Staple the dry fabric edges together and apply resin only to the top layer
choices: A. Leave a half-inch gap between fabric edges so pure resin fills the seam
B. Overlap seams by 1 to 3 inches and stagger the overlaps between layers
C. Stack all overlaps directly on top of one another to create a thick ridge
D. Staple the dry fabric edges together and apply resin only to the top layer
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Overlap seams by 1 to 3 inches and stagger the overlaps between layers
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Overlapping fiberglass seams by 1 to 3 inches preserves laminate strength, and staggering overlaps across multiple layers prevents thick buildups that create weak spots (p. 60).

Meals prepared for rank advancement or other merit badges may not be counted toward the Cooking merit badge. Menus used for meals in requirements 4, 5, and 6 must not be repeated. Outdoor Cooking: Where local regulations do not allow you to build a fire, the counselor may adjust the requirement to meet the law. The meals in requirements 5 and 6 may be prepared for different trips and need not be prepared consecutively. Scouts working on this badge in summer camp should take into consideration foods that can be obtained at the camp commissary.

requirements.lead_text: Health and safety. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Health and safety. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in cooking activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Show that you know first aid for and how to prevent injuries or illnesses that could occur while preparing meals and eating, including burns and scalds, cuts, choking, and allergic reactions. (c) Describe how meat, fish, chicken, eggs, dairy products, and fresh vegetables should be stored, transported, and properly prepared for cooking. Explain how to prevent cross-contamination. (d) Discuss with your counselor food allergies, food intolerance, and food-related illnesses and diseases. Explain why someone who handles or prepares food needs to be aware of these concerns. (e) Discuss with your counselor why reading food labels is important. Explain how to identify common allergens such as peanuts, tree nuts, milk, eggs, wheat, soy, and shellfish.

pamphlet_excerpts: Prioritizing Kitchen Safety: Safety is always a Scout's primary consideration (p. 64).
Emergency Injury Readiness: All good cooks should be prepared to take action should an injury occur (p. 64).
Cross-Contamination Prevention: They must know how to properly prepare and store foods to help prevent cross-contamination and avoid the spread of food-related illnesses (p. 64).
Recognizing Allergic Reactions: They should also be able to identify when individuals become sick because of an illness or allergic reaction (p. 64).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Separate Raw and Cooked: They must know how to properly prepare and store foods to help prevent cross-contamination and avoid the spread of food-related illnesses (p. 64).
Step 2 - Watch for Illness Symptoms: They should also be able to identify when individuals become sick because of an illness or allergic reaction (p. 64).
Step 3 - Follow Kitchen Safety Rules: Following the safety guidelines presented here will not eliminate your risk of a cooking injury but will help prepare you in case (p. 64).
Step 4 - Apply Basic First Aid: Basic first-aid techniques should be used when someone is injured while cooking (p. 64).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: While preparing chicken fajitas at camp, a Scout uses a plastic cutting board and chef's knife to slice raw chicken breast, and then reaches for fresh bell peppers and tortillas to slice for a cold side salad. What food-safety step is required first?
quiz_item.question: While preparing chicken fajitas at camp, a Scout uses a plastic cutting board and chef's knife to slice raw chicken breast, and then reaches for fresh bell peppers and tortillas to slice for a cold side salad. What food-safety step is required first?
options: A. Wipe the knife blade on a dry camp towel and slice the raw vegetables on the same board.

B. Prevent cross-contamination by using a separate cutting board for produce, or washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the board, knife, and hands thoroughly with hot soapy water and sanitizer solution before touching ready-to-eat food.
C. Leave the raw chicken sitting in the sun at 75°F for 4 hours before cooking.
D. Rinse the cutting board briefly in cold creek water without soap or sanitizer.
choices: A. Wipe the knife blade on a dry camp towel and slice the raw vegetables on the same board.

B. Prevent cross-contamination by using a separate cutting board for produce, or washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the board, knife, and hands thoroughly with hot soapy water and sanitizer solution before touching ready-to-eat food.
C. Leave the raw chicken sitting in the sun at 75°F for 4 hours before cooking.
D. Rinse the cutting board briefly in cold creek water without soap or sanitizer.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Prevent cross-contamination by using a separate cutting board for produce, or washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the board, knife, and hands thoroughly with hot soapy water and sanitizer solution before touching ready-to-eat food.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Raw poultry carries Salmonella and Campylobacter; transferring raw juices to ready-to-eat produce causes acute foodborne illness unless surfaces are sanitized and perishables stay out of the 40°F-140°F danger zone.

requirements.req_text: Nutrition. Then, based on the MyPlate food guide, discuss with your counselor an appropriate meal plan for yourself for one day. (d) Discuss your current eating habits with your counselor and what you can do to eat healthier, based on the MyPlate food guide. quiz_item.question: Why is a cast-iron Dutch oven particularly well suited for slow simmering and baking in a camp kitchen?
options: A. Its thin aluminum walls cool down immediately when removed from coals
B. Its ultralight weight makes it ideal for solo long-distance backpacking
C. Its thick cast-iron walls distribute and hold heat evenly around the food
D. It requires no preheating or seasoning before cooking acidic stews
choices: A. Its thin aluminum walls cool down immediately when removed from coals
B. Its ultralight weight makes it ideal for solo long-distance backpacking
C. Its thick cast-iron walls distribute and hold heat evenly around the food
D. It requires no preheating or seasoning before cooking acidic stews
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Its thick cast-iron walls distribute and hold heat evenly around the food
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A Dutch oven has thick walls that retain and distribute heat evenly, making it ideal for baking, roasting, and slow simmering at camp (p. 24).

requirements.lead_text: Cooking at Home. Do the following: Note: The meals for requirement 4 may be prepared on different days, and they need not be prepared consecutively. The requirement calls for Scouts to plan, prepare, and serve one breakfast, one lunch, and one dinner to at least one adult; those served need not be the same for all meals.
requirements.req_text: Cooking at Home. Do the following: Note: The meals for requirement 4 may be prepared on different days, and they need not be prepared consecutively. The requirement calls for Scouts to plan, prepare, and serve one breakfast, one lunch, and one dinner to at least one adult; those served need not be the same for all meals. (a) Using the MyPlate food guide or the current USDA nutrition model, plan menus for three full days of meals (three breakfasts, three lunches, and three dinners) plus one dessert. Your menus should include enough to feed yourself and at least one adult, keeping in mind any special needs (such as food allergies) and how you keep your foods safe and free from cross-contamination. List the equipment and utensils needed to prepare and serve these meals. (b) Find recipes for each meal. Create a shopping list for your meals showing the amount of food needed to prepare for the number of people you will serve. Determine the cost for each meal. (c) Share and discuss your meal plan and shopping list with your counselor. (d) Using at least five of the 10 cooking methods from requirement 3, prepare and serve yourself and at least one adult (parent, family member, guardian, or other responsible adult) one breakfast, one lunch, one dinner, and one dessert from the meals you planned. (e) Time your cooking to have each meal ready to serve at the proper time. Have an adult verify the preparation of the meal to your counselor. (f) After each meal, ask a person you served to evaluate the meal on presentation and taste, then evaluate your own meal. Discuss what you learned with your counselor, including any adjustments that could have improved or enhanced your meals. Tell how planning and preparation help ensure a successful meal.

requirements.lead_text: Camp Cooking. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Camp Cooking. Do the following: (a) Using the MyPlate food guide or the current USDA nutrition model, plan a menu that includes four meals, one snack, and one dessert for your patrol (or a similar size group of up to eight youth, including you) on a camping trip. These four meals must include two breakfasts, one lunch, and one dinner. Additionally, you must plan one snack and one dessert. Your menus should include enough food for each person, keeping in mind any special needs (such as food allergies) and how you keep your foods safe and free from cross-contamination. List the equipment and utensils needed to prepare and serve these meals. (b) Find or create recipes for the four meals, the snack, and the dessert you have planned. Adjust menu items in the recipes for the number to be served. Create a shopping list and budget to determine the per-person cost. (c) Share and discuss your menu plans and shopping list with your counselor. (d) In the outdoors, using your menu plans and recipes for this requirement, cook two of the four meals you planned using either a camp stove OR backpacking stove. Use a skillet OR a Dutch oven over campfire coals for the third meal, and cook the fourth meal in a foil pack OR on a skewer. Serve all of these meals to your patrol or a group of youth. (e) In the outdoors, using your menu plans and recipes for this requirement, prepare one snack and one dessert. Serve both of these to your patrol or a group of youth. (f) After each meal, have those you served evaluate the meal on presentation and taste, and then evaluate your own meal. Discuss what you learned with your counselor, including any adjustments that could have improved or enhanced your meals. Tell how planning and preparation help ensure successful outdoor cooking. (g) Lead the clean-up of equipment, utensils, and the cooking site thoroughly after each meal. Properly store or dispose of unused ingredients, leftover food, dishwater and garbage. (h) Discuss how you followed the Leave No Trace Seven Principles and the Outdoor Code when preparing your meals.

requirements.lead_text: Trail and Backpacking Meals. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Trail and Backpacking Meals. Do the following: (a) Using the MyPlate food guide or the current USDA nutrition model, plan a day of meals for trail hiking or backpacking that includes one breakfast, one lunch, one dinner, and one snack. These meals must consider weight, not require refrigeration and are to be consumed by three to five people (including you). List the equipment and utensils needed to prepare and serve these meals. (b) Create a shopping list for your meals, showing the amount of food needed to prepare and serve each meal, and the cost for each meal. (c) Share and discuss your menu and shopping list with your counselor. Your plan must include how to repackage foods for your hike or backpacking trip to eliminate as much bulk, weight, and garbage as possible. (d) While on a trail hike or backpacking trip, prepare and serve two meals and a snack from the menu planned for this requirement. At least one of those meals must be cooked over a fire, or an approved trail stove (with proper supervision). (e) After each meal, have those you served evaluate the meal on presentation and taste, then evaluate your own meal. Discuss what you learned with your counselor, including any adjustments that could have improved or enhanced your meals. Tell how planning and preparation help ensure successful trail hiking or backpacking meals. (f) Explain to your counselor how you should divide the food and cooking supplies among the patrol in order to share the load. Discuss how to properly clean the cooking area and store your food to protect it from animals.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: While preparing chicken fajitas at camp, a Scout uses a plastic cutting board and chef's knife to slice raw chicken breast, and then reaches for fresh bell peppers and tortillas to slice for a cold side salad. What food-safety step is required first?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: While preparing chicken fajitas at camp, a Scout uses a plastic cutting board and chef's knife to slice raw chicken breast, and then reaches for fresh bell peppers and tortillas to slice for a cold side salad. What food-safety step is required first?
options: A. Wipe the knife blade on a dry camp towel and slice the raw vegetables on the same board.

B. Prevent cross-contamination by using a separate cutting board for produce, or washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the board, knife, and hands thoroughly with hot soapy water and sanitizer solution before touching ready-to-eat food.
C. Leave the raw chicken sitting in the sun at 75°F for 4 hours before cooking.
D. Rinse the cutting board briefly in cold creek water without soap or sanitizer.
choices: A. Wipe the knife blade on a dry camp towel and slice the raw vegetables on the same board.

B. Prevent cross-contamination by using a separate cutting board for produce, or washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the board, knife, and hands thoroughly with hot soapy water and sanitizer solution before touching ready-to-eat food.
C. Leave the raw chicken sitting in the sun at 75°F for 4 hours before cooking.
D. Rinse the cutting board briefly in cold creek water without soap or sanitizer.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Prevent cross-contamination by using a separate cutting board for produce, or washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the board, knife, and hands thoroughly with hot soapy water and sanitizer solution before touching ready-to-eat food.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Raw poultry carries Salmonella and Campylobacter; transferring raw juices to ready-to-eat produce causes acute foodborne illness unless surfaces are sanitized and perishables stay out of the 40°F-140°F danger zone.

choices: A. About 2,200 calories per day

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. About 2,200 calories per day
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The USDA daily food plan recommends about 2,200 calories per day for an average 12-year-old male who gets 30 to 60 minutes of daily exercise, including 7 ounces of grains, 3 cups of vegetables, 2 cups of fruit, 3 cups of dairy, and 6 ounces of protein (p. 54).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is a cast-iron Dutch oven particularly well suited for slow simmering and baking in a camp kitchen?
options: A. Its thin aluminum walls cool down immediately when removed from coals
B. Its ultralight weight makes it ideal for solo long-distance backpacking
C. Its thick cast-iron walls distribute and hold heat evenly around the food
D. It requires no preheating or seasoning before cooking acidic stews
choices: A. Its thin aluminum walls cool down immediately when removed from coals
B. Its ultralight weight makes it ideal for solo long-distance backpacking
C. Its thick cast-iron walls distribute and hold heat evenly around the food
D. It requires no preheating or seasoning before cooking acidic stews
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Its thick cast-iron walls distribute and hold heat evenly around the food
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A Dutch oven has thick walls that retain and distribute heat evenly, making it ideal for baking, roasting, and slow simmering at camp (p. 24).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How should a patrol handle food scraps and wash water when cleaning up a camp kitchen under Leave No Trace principles?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How should a patrol handle food scraps and wash water when cleaning up a camp kitchen under Leave No Trace principles?
options: A. Wash pots directly in a creek so flowing water carries bits downstream
B. Bury leftover food scraps six inches deep next to the tent site
C. Burn all aluminum foil and wet food waste in the campfire ring
D. Strain food particles into sealed trash bags to pack out and scatter wastewater away from water sources
choices: A. Wash pots directly in a creek so flowing water carries bits downstream
B. Bury leftover food scraps six inches deep next to the tent site

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Strain food particles into sealed trash bags to pack out and scatter wastewater away from water sources
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Following Leave No Trace and the Outdoor Code requires straining food particles out of dishwater, packing out all solid waste, and disposing of wash water properly away from natural water sources (p. 50).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Crime Prevention Requirement 1, how does Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) reduce neighborhood property crime without relying on vigilante action?
quiz_item.question: In Crime Prevention Requirement 1, how does Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) reduce neighborhood property crime without relying on vigilante action?
options: A. By encouraging youths to patrol dark alleys alone at midnight and confront suspicious strangers directly.
B. By planting dense, eight-foot hedges directly over front windows and turning off all exterior porch and street lighting.

C. By trimming overgrown shrubs around doors and windows to create clear sightlines (natural surveillance), installing motion-activated exterior lighting, securing deadbolts, and organizing a Neighborhood Watch that promptly reports suspicious activity to police.
D. By leaving garage doors open during the day and hiding spare house keys under the front doormat for convenience.
choices: A. By encouraging youths to patrol dark alleys alone at midnight and confront suspicious strangers directly.
B. By planting dense, eight-foot hedges directly over front windows and turning off all exterior porch and street lighting.

C. By trimming overgrown shrubs around doors and windows to create clear sightlines (natural surveillance), installing motion-activated exterior lighting, securing deadbolts, and organizing a Neighborhood Watch that promptly reports suspicious activity to police.
D. By leaving garage doors open during the day and hiding spare house keys under the front doormat for convenience.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. By trimming overgrown shrubs around doors and windows to create clear sightlines (natural surveillance), installing motion-activated exterior lighting, securing deadbolts, and organizing a Neighborhood Watch that promptly reports suspicious activity to police.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): CPTED deters burglars by increasing visibility (clear sightlines and lighting), reinforcing physical access controls (deadbolts and window locks), and pairing safe design with observation-only Neighborhood Watch reporting to law enforcement.

pamphlet_excerpts: Drug Induced Violent Behavior: Bizarre behavior while under the influence of cocaine can unwittingly lead to fatal accidents and to violence such as suicide or murder (p. 7).
Severe Chemical Burn Hazards: Freebasing (heating cocaine to dissolve it) often causes severe burn accidents (p. 7).
Processed Freebase Cocaine Forms: Crack cocaine (also known as "crack," "rock," and "ready rock") is cocaine that has been processed from cocainehydrochloride to a freebase for smoking (p. 7).
Origin of Crack Terminology: The term "crack" refers to the crackling sound heard when the mixture is heated ("smoked") (p. 7).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Identify Illicit Street Drugs: Crack cocaine (also known as "crack," "rock," and "ready rock") is cocaine that has been processed from cocainehydrochloride to a freebase for smoking (p. 7).
Step 2 - Recognize Drug Processing Hazards: The term "crack" refers to the crackling sound heard when the mixture is heated ("smoked") (p. 7).
Step 3 - Learn Narcotic Slang Terms: Common names for heroin include "dust," "H," "horse," "junk," and "smack." A user becomes dependent even with occasional abuse and in low doses (p. 7).
Step 4 - Spot Dangerous Physical Symptoms: Effects of heroin include irregular breathing and heartbeat (p. 7).

Core Definition of Crime: Crime is the violation of a law, a duty, or a moral principle (p. 7).
Prosecution and Legal Punishment: Those arrested by law enforcement officers for committing crimes face prosecution and punishment (p. 7).
Proactive Family Prevention Steps: In this pamphlet, you will learn about the different types of crimes and steps that you, and your family and neighbors, can take to help prevent (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Crime Prevention Requirement 1, how does Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) reduce neighborhood property crime without relying on vigilante action?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Crime Prevention Requirement 1, how does Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) reduce neighborhood property crime without relying on vigilante action?
options: A. By encouraging youths to patrol dark alleys alone at midnight and confront suspicious strangers directly.
B. By planting dense, eight-foot hedges directly over front windows and turning off all exterior porch and street lighting.

C. By trimming overgrown shrubs around doors and windows to create clear sightlines (natural surveillance), installing motion-activated exterior lighting, securing deadbolts, and organizing a Neighborhood Watch that promptly reports suspicious activity to police.
D. By leaving garage doors open during the day and hiding spare house keys under the front doormat for convenience.
choices: A. By encouraging youths to patrol dark alleys alone at midnight and confront suspicious strangers directly.
B. By planting dense, eight-foot hedges directly over front windows and turning off all exterior porch and street lighting.

C. By trimming overgrown shrubs around doors and windows to create clear sightlines (natural surveillance), installing motion-activated exterior lighting, securing deadbolts, and organizing a Neighborhood Watch that promptly reports suspicious activity to police.
D. By leaving garage doors open during the day and hiding spare house keys under the front doormat for convenience.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. By trimming overgrown shrubs around doors and windows to create clear sightlines (natural surveillance), installing motion-activated exterior lighting, securing deadbolts, and organizing a Neighborhood Watch that promptly reports suspicious activity to police.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): CPTED deters burglars by increasing visibility (clear sightlines and lighting), reinforcing physical access controls (deadbolts and window locks), and pairing safe design with observation-only Neighborhood Watch reporting to law enforcement.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Cybersecurity Requirement 1, how do the three pillars of the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) protect an organization's information systems?
quiz_item.question: In Cybersecurity Requirement 1, how do the three pillars of the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) protect an organization's information systems?
options: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
B. Confidentiality means keeping software bugs secret from programmers, Integrity means never updating operating systems, and Availability means posting all employee passwords on a public webpage.
C. The CIA Triad requires sharing a single administrator password across all staff members so nobody is ever locked out of the network.
D. Confidentiality deletes all files after twenty-four hours, Integrity blocks antivirus scanners, and Availability disables multi-factor authentication.
choices: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
B. Confidentiality means keeping software bugs secret from programmers, Integrity means never updating operating systems, and Availability means posting all employee passwords on a public webpage.
C. The CIA Triad requires sharing a single administrator password across all staff members so nobody is ever locked out of the network.
D. Confidentiality deletes all files after twenty-four hours, Integrity blocks antivirus scanners, and Availability disables multi-factor authentication.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The CIA Triad is the core model of information security: Confidentiality protects privacy, Integrity guards accuracy and trustworthiness against tampering, and Availability keeps systems operational for legitimate users.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: If an attacker secretly alters the account balances in a bank database without stealing the data or taking the server offline, which principle of the C.I.A. Triad was primarily violated?
quiz_item.question: If an attacker secretly alters the account balances in a bank database without stealing the data or taking the server offline, which principle of the C.I.A. Triad was primarily violated?
options: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
B. Confidentiality, because the website was temporarily unreachable during the afternoon
C. Availability, because an unauthorized person read private messages without changing them
D. Non-repudiation, because the server hardware ran out of backup battery power
choices: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
B. Confidentiality, because the website was temporarily unreachable during the afternoon
C. Availability, because an unauthorized person read private messages without changing them
D. Non-repudiation, because the server hardware ran out of backup battery power
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Integrity ensures that data remains accurate, complete, and unaltered by unauthorized users while stored or in transit (p. 6).

requirements.lead_text: Cyber Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks. Do the following and discuss each with your counselor:
requirements.req_text: Cyber Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks. Do the following and discuss each with your counselor: (a) Define the terms vulnerability, threat, and exploit, and give an example of each that might apply to a website or software product you use. (b) Pick one type of malware (such as virus, worm, Trojan, backdoor, spyware, or ransomware) and find out how it works. Explain what it does and the harm it can cause. (c) Identify two risks of using public Wi-Fi and describe how to reduce or avoid those risks. (d) Describe what spoofing and phishing are, and how to recognize a message or website that might be trying to trick you. Explain what steps you should take to protect yourself and others if you come across one. (e) Current Events. Do ONE of the following: (1) Read an article or a news report about a recent cybersecurity incident, such as a data breach or malware infection. Explain how the incident happened (to the best of your ability based on the information available) and what the consequences are or might be to the victim. (2) With your parent or guardian's permission, watch a movie or read a book in which cybersecurity plays a significant role. Discuss how cybersecurity topics were depicted and how realistic you think it was. (f) Create a list of what is part of your cyber attack surface including all the ways someone could try to access your personal information or devices, such as online accounts, apps, or home networks.

common_misconception_pair.fact: A vulnerability is a weakness in software or configuration, a threat is a potential danger or actor that could cause harm, and an exploit is the specific tool or attack technique used to take advantage of that weakness (p. 7).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is a primary risk of connecting to an open public Wi-Fi hotspot at a coffee shop, and how can you reduce that risk?
quiz_item.question: What is a primary risk of connecting to an open public Wi-Fi hotspot at a coffee shop, and how can you reduce that risk?
options: A. Public Wi-Fi signals drain laptop batteries faster and corrupt local hard drive sectors
B. Public routers automatically install ransomware onto every device that connects without a password
C. Turning off your device firewall on public Wi-Fi is required so encrypted websites load properly
D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
choices: A. Public Wi-Fi signals drain laptop batteries faster and corrupt local hard drive sectors
B. Public routers automatically install ransomware onto every device that connects without a password
C. Turning off your device firewall on public Wi-Fi is required so encrypted websites load properly
D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Public Wi-Fi networks allow attackers on the same network to intercept unencrypted traffic or set up evil-twin rogue hotspots; using a VPN and HTTPS websites protects your data in transit (p. 7).

requirements.lead_text: Cyber Defenses. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Cyber Defenses. Do the following: (a) Describe three technologies that are used to defend a computer or network, such as access controls, antivirus software, firewall, intrusion detection/prevention systems, and Virtual Private Network. (b) Installing updates. Do the following: (1) Explain to your counselor the importance of installing the latest updates on your computer, why they are needed, and what kinds of problems they can prevent. (2) Demonstrate to your counselor how to check for, download, and install the latest updates for your computer or mobile device, or another computer you have permission to use. (If you are unable to do this on your computer, you may use an online guide with screenshots to demonstrate this.) Show your counselor how to verify that your computer or mobile device is up-to-date. (c) System security. With your parent or guardian's permission, do THREE of the following using a computer or mobile device, and discuss with your counselor: (1) Describe what makes a good password and why. Set or change an account password to one that is "strong." (2) Describe multi-factor authentication (MFA) and how it can be used to improve security. Demonstrate how to use an authenticator app or other MFA function. (3) Install and set up a password manager. Demonstrate how it works to your counselor. (4) Run a virus scan. Show the results to your counselor. (5) Using a command line or other built-in tool, see what programs or processes are running on your computer. Discuss with your counselor what you see and what surprises you. (6) Use a command line interface to view your computer's open network connections. Discuss the results with your counselor. (7) Demonstrate how to back up your data from a mobile device to a local computer or the cloud. (8) Research best practices for protecting a home computer or network, and make a checklist of FIVE things you and your family can do to stay secure. (9) Identify one or more other vulnerabilities on your home computer or network or another computer or network you have permission to use and discuss with your counselor. With permission from the system owner, take the necessary actions to fix it.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: System security. With your parent or guardian's permission, do THREE of the following using a computer or mobile device, and discuss with your counselor: (1) Describe what makes a good password and why. Set or change an account password to one that is "strong." (2) Describe multi-factor authentication (MFA) and how it can be used to improve security. Demonstrate how to use an authenticator app or other MFA function. (3) Install and set up a password manager. Demonstrate how it works to your counselor. (4) Run a virus scan. Show the results to your counselor. (5) Using a command line or other built-in tool, see what programs or processes are running on your computer. Discuss with your counselor what you see and what surprises you. (6) Use a command line interface to view your computer's open network connections. Discuss the results with your counselor. (7) Demonstrate how to back up your data from a mobile device to a local computer or the cloud. (8) Research best practices for protecting a home computer or network, and make a checklist of FIVE things you and your family can do to stay secure. (9) Identify one or more other vulnerabilities on your home computer or network or another computer or network you have permission to use and discuss with your counselor. With permission from the system owner, take the necessary actions to fix.

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Software updates and security patches fix newly discovered vulnerabilities in operating systems and applications before attackers can exploit them (p. 8).

requirements.lead_text: Cryptography. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Cryptography. Do the following: (a) Research and explain to your counselor three situations where encryption is used in cybersecurity. For each situation, describe what kind of encryption is used and why it is important. (b) Show how you can know if your connection to a website is encrypted. (c) Do ONE of the following: (1) Create your own encryption code, such as a substitution cipher or code book, and demonstrate using it to encrypt and decrypt a message. Describe the strengths and weaknesses of your code. (2) Download and set up an app (from an official app store) that uses end-to-end encryption. Explain to your counselor what this means, how it works, and why it is more secure than other forms of communication (e. g. SMS). (3) Use a hashing tool (for example, using SHA or MD5) to create a checksum for a file, document, or piece of text. Have a fellow Scout or your counselor make a change to it, then recreate the checksum and compare the new checksum to the original as a demonstration of file integrity checking. (4) Create your own PGP (pretty good privacy) email key. Share your public key with others (and your counselor). Also, get their public keys and add them to your computer's key ring. Send a message that has been digitally encrypted.

D. The website loads in less than two seconds without showing any pop-up advertisements

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The browser address bar uses https:// and displays a valid TLS security certificate for that domain
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): An HTTPS URL with a valid TLS/SSL security certificate in the browser address bar indicates that traffic between your browser and the website is encrypted in transit (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Cybersecurity Requirement 1, how do the three pillars of the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) protect an organization's information systems?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Cybersecurity Requirement 1, how do the three pillars of the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) protect an organization's information systems?
options: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
B. Confidentiality means keeping software bugs secret from programmers, Integrity means never updating operating systems, and Availability means posting all employee passwords on a public webpage.
C. The CIA Triad requires sharing a single administrator password across all staff members so nobody is ever locked out of the network.
D. Confidentiality deletes all files after twenty-four hours, Integrity blocks antivirus scanners, and Availability disables multi-factor authentication.
choices: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
B. Confidentiality means keeping software bugs secret from programmers, Integrity means never updating operating systems, and Availability means posting all employee passwords on a public webpage.
C. The CIA Triad requires sharing a single administrator password across all staff members so nobody is ever locked out of the network.
D. Confidentiality deletes all files after twenty-four hours, Integrity blocks antivirus scanners, and Availability disables multi-factor authentication.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The CIA Triad is the core model of information security: Confidentiality protects privacy, Integrity guards accuracy and trustworthiness against tampering, and Availability keeps systems operational for legitimate users.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: If an attacker secretly alters the account balances in a bank database without stealing the data or taking the server offline, which principle of the C.I.A. Triad was primarily violated?
options: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
B. Confidentiality, because the website was temporarily unreachable during the afternoon
C. Availability, because an unauthorized person read private messages without changing them
D. Non-repudiation, because the server hardware ran out of backup battery power
choices: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
B. Confidentiality, because the website was temporarily unreachable during the afternoon
C. Availability, because an unauthorized person read private messages without changing them
D. Non-repudiation, because the server hardware ran out of backup battery power
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Integrity ensures that data remains accurate, complete, and unaltered by unauthorized users while stored or in transit (p. 6).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is a primary risk of connecting to an open public Wi-Fi hotspot at a coffee shop, and how can you reduce that risk?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is a primary risk of connecting to an open public Wi-Fi hotspot at a coffee shop, and how can you reduce that risk?
options: A. Public Wi-Fi signals drain laptop batteries faster and corrupt local hard drive sectors
B. Public routers automatically install ransomware onto every device that connects without a password
C. Turning off your device firewall on public Wi-Fi is required so encrypted websites load properly
D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
choices: A. Public Wi-Fi signals drain laptop batteries faster and corrupt local hard drive sectors
B. Public routers automatically install ransomware onto every device that connects without a password
C. Turning off your device firewall on public Wi-Fi is required so encrypted websites load properly
D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Public Wi-Fi networks allow attackers on the same network to intercept unencrypted traffic or set up evil-twin rogue hotspots; using a VPN and HTTPS websites protects your data in transit (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is enabling automatic operating system and application updates one of the most effective cyber defenses?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is enabling automatic operating system and application updates one of the most effective cyber defenses?
options: A. They only add new cosmetic icons and slow down older computers without improving security
B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
C. They automatically delete all your personal documents to free up hard drive space every month
D. They replace the need for strong passwords and multi-factor authentication on web accounts
choices: A. They only add new cosmetic icons and slow down older computers without improving security
B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
C. They automatically delete all your personal documents to free up hard drive space every month
D. They replace the need for strong passwords and multi-factor authentication on web accounts
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Software updates and security patches fix newly discovered vulnerabilities in operating systems and applications before attackers can exploit them (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How can you verify that your connection to a website is encrypted before entering login credentials or payment details?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How can you verify that your connection to a website is encrypted before entering login credentials or payment details?
options: A. The website page background uses dark mode and displays a copyright notice at the bottom
B. The website URL ends with .org or .com instead of an IP address
C. The browser address bar uses https:// and displays a valid TLS security certificate for that domain
D. The website loads in less than two seconds without showing any pop-up advertisements
choices: A. The website page background uses dark mode and displays a copyright notice at the bottom
B. The website URL ends with .org or .com instead of an IP address
C. The browser address bar uses https:// and displays a valid TLS security certificate for that domain
D. The website loads in less than two seconds without showing any pop-up advertisements
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The browser address bar uses https:// and displays a valid TLS security certificate for that domain
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): An HTTPS URL with a valid TLS/SSL security certificate in the browser address bar indicates that traffic between your browser and the website is encrypted in transit (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which set of steps best secures connected Internet of Things (IoT) devices in your home?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which set of steps best secures connected Internet of Things (IoT) devices in your home?
options: A. Change default passwords immediately, keep device firmware updated, and isolate IoT devices on a separate network segment
B. Leave the factory password unchanged so the manufacturer can log in and repair the device remotely
C. Forward all router ports directly to the smart camera so you can view it without a password
D. Connect smart devices to your neighbor's open Wi-Fi network so your own router stays hidden
choices: A. Change default passwords immediately, keep device firmware updated, and isolate IoT devices on a separate network segment
B. Leave the factory password unchanged so the manufacturer can log in and repair the device remotely
C. Forward all router ports directly to the smart camera so you can view it without a password
D. Connect smart devices to your neighbor's open Wi-Fi network so your own router stays hidden
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Change default passwords immediately, keep device firmware updated, and isolate IoT devices on a separate network segment
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Changing factory-default passwords, installing firmware updates, disabling unneeded remote access, and placing IoT devices on a separate guest Wi-Fi network protect your home network (p. 6).

pamphlet_excerpts: Cleaning Minor Cuts and Scrapes: Wash cuts, scratches, and scrapes with soap and water (p. 86).
Sterile Dressing for Larger Wounds: Cover larger wounds with a sterile gauzepad or a clean cloth folded into a pad (p. 86).
Long-Term Risks of Sun Exposure: Sunburn can cause lasting skin damage and the potential for skin cancer (p. 86).
Sunscreen and Protective Riding Apparel: Cover up to prevent sunburn, and use plenty of sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15 (p. 86).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Assess Sunburn and Heat Risks: Sunburn can cause lasting skin damage and the potential for skin cancer (p. 86).
Step 2 - Apply SPF 15 Sunscreen Protection: Cover up to prevent sunburn, and use plenty of sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15 (p. 86).
Step 3 - Cool Sunburned Skin With Cloths: To ease the pain of a mild sunburn, apply cool, wet cloths to the affected area (p. 86).
Step 4 - Soothe Skin With Aloe Lotion: A soothing lotion containing chamomile or aloe vera may provide relief (p. 86).

common_misconception_pair.misconception: The safest way to mount and start a bike is to sit high on the saddle on tiptoes or run alongside the rolling bike and jump onto the seat.
common_misconception_pair.fact: To start smoothly, straddle the top tube with brakes engaged, rotate the starting pedal backward to the 10 o'clock power position, release the brakes, and push down on the pedal while rising onto the saddle (p. 53).
common_misconception_pair.fact_correction: To start smoothly, straddle the top tube with brakes engaged, rotate the starting pedal backward to the 10 o'clock power position, release the brakes, and push down on the pedal while rising onto the saddle (p. 53).
