pamphlet_excerpts: Locking Brakes Before Mounting: To mount the bicycle, engage the brakes to prevent the bike from rolling (p. 53).
Straddling the Bicycle Top Tube: Swing either leg up and over the bike and straddle the top tube (p. 53).
Pedal Power Position at Ten O'Clock: Use your foot to turn the crank backward until it reaches the 10 o'clock position (p. 53).
Smooth Transition Onto the Saddle: As your body moves up and the bike moves forward, the saddle will move (p. 53).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Set Crank at Ten O'Clock: Use your foot to turn the crank backward until it reaches the 10 o'clock position (p. 53).
Step 2 - Push Down and Rise Onto Saddle: As your body moves up and the bike moves forward, the saddle will move (p. 53).
Step 3 - Complete Second Pedal Stroke Smoothly: When the opposite pedal reaches the 12 o'clock position, make a second pedal stroke (p. 53).
Step 4 - Dismount Using Low Left Pedal: To dismount, place the left pedal straight down and stand on it like a step (p. 53).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the proper technique for executing an emergency stop on a bicycle without pitching over the handlebars?
quiz_item.question: What is the proper technique for executing an emergency stop on a bicycle without pitching over the handlebars?
options: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
choices: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): During an emergency stop, applying both brakes firmly while shifting your hips and body weight low and back over the rear wheel maximizes stopping power and prevents pitching over the handlebars (p. 53).

requirements.lead_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website)
requirements.req_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website) (a) Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride. (b) Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride.

sub_requirements.label: (b)
sub_requirements.text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner
D. Shift your shoulders far behind the rear tire while turning the handlebars sharply without leaning the bicycle frame
choices: A. Sit back heavily on the saddle, drop the inside pedal to the ground, and lock the rear brake through the apex

C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner

intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-11-01). Dancing is a fun and exciting way to express yourself, stay active, and connect with others. Every style of dance, from hip hop and ballet to cultural and partner dances, has its own rhythm, history, and story to tell. In the Dance Test Lab Badge, you’ll learn how to move safely, warm up properly, and understand what makes every dance unique. You’ll explore different styles of dance, learn about famous dancers, and even perform your own routine. Whether you’re new to dancing or already love it, this badge will help you build confidence, creativity, and coordination while having a great time moving to the beat.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

requirements.lead_text: Preventing Injury. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Preventing Injury. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor how you can prevent injuries while participating in dancing activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. Explain what you need to take into consideration before trying potentially dangerous moves including but not limited to jumps, flips, and lifts. (b) Explain to your counselor how to appropriately warm-up prior to dancing activities to protect joints and prevent injury. Demonstrate three dance warm-ups. (c) Show that you know first aid for injuries that could occur while dancing, including cuts, scratches, abrasions, concussions, blisters, sprains, stress fractures, tendonitis, and back injuries. (d) Explain the importance of wearing the right clothing and gear for dance, including appropriate footwear.

pamphlet_excerpts: Anticipating Dance Hazards: Explain to your counselor how you can prevent injuries while participating in dancing activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate (p. 4).
Joint Protection Warmups: Explain to your counselor how to appropriately warm-up prior to dancing activities to protect joints and prevent injury. Demonstrate three dance warm-ups (p. 4).
Treating Dance Injuries: Show that you know first aid for injuries that could occur while dancing, including cuts, scratches, abrasions, concussions, blisters, sprains, stress fractures (p. 4).
Proper Footwear Selection: Explain the importance of wearing the right clothing and gear for dance, including appropriate footwear (p. 4).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Demonstrate Injury First Aid: Show that you know first aid for injuries that could occur while dancing, including cuts, scratches, abrasions, concussions, blisters, sprains, stress fractures (p. 4).
Step 2 - Select Proper Dance Gear: Explain the importance of wearing the right clothing and gear for dance, including appropriate footwear (p. 4).
Step 3 - Practice Warmups With Buddy: Cross-check your Dance Injury Prevention, Warm-Ups & First Aid technique, measurements, and results with a patrol buddy using the EDGE method (p. 10).
Step 4 - Review Safety With Counselor: Review your completed Dance Injury Prevention, Warm-Ups & First Aid evidence and demonstrate proficiency during your counselor conference (p. 10).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
quiz_item.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
choices: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dynamic warm-ups increase muscle elasticity and joint synovial fluid, while a clean, dry sprung floor prevents ankle sprains and falls.

quiz_item.question: When a choreographer contrasts a sharp, sudden punch with a slow, floating arm sweep, which element of dance is primarily being varied?
options: A. Floor pathway
B. Energy
C. Group formation
D. Stage lighting
choices: A. Floor pathway
B. Energy
C. Group formation
D. Stage lighting
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Energy
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Energy governs how movement happens, distinguishing between percussive, sustained, swinging, suspended, or collapsing movement qualities (p. 10).

requirements.lead_text: Research. Research TWO of the types of dance you learned about in requirement 3 by doing the following for EACH type of dance you chose:
requirements.req_text: Research. Research TWO of the types of dance you learned about in requirement 3 by doing the following for EACH type of dance you chose: (a) Give a brief history, including its origin, how it came to be in the United States if it originated elsewhere, and where in the world/country it is most often performed. (b) Name/describe different variations of this style of dancing, if any. (c) Name some specific types of dance steps/moves particular to this type of dance. Does this dance tell a story through movement? If so, please describe. (d) Include information on at least one person who became well-known performing, teaching, or choreographing this type of dance. (e) Note if anyone with a physical disability (such a person with hearing or sight impairment or a person who uses a wheelchair) could participate in this type of dancing. What accommodations would that person need to participate? (f) Locate and share a place near you/in your state where you could watch or participate in this type of dance as a part of a performance, competition, or class. Find out when and where this is offered and what the cost would be to watch or participate. (g) Watch a performance of this type of dance and discuss with your counselor. (While viewing an in-person performance is preferable, a recorded performance may also be permitted.)

requirements.lead_text: Learn and Perform a Dance. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Learn and Perform a Dance. Do the following: (a) Learn a dance. Use at least THREE types of warm-ups prior to your routine to prepare different muscle groups for the exercise. The dance may be solo, group, or partner dance and can use a memorized choreographed routine or an improvised dance. It should be a minimum of 2 minutes long or several shorter dances that add up to at least 2 minutes. The dance should demonstrate at least three different dance moves/steps and should contain music with Scout-appropriate lyrics, if applicable. (b) Perform the dance for your counselor or submit a video of your performance to your counselor. Describe to your counselor what precautions you took to avoid injury before and during your performance. Name or describe the 3 different dance moves that you learned, the 3 different warm-ups you chose, and the 5 Elements of Dance in your routine.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
choices: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dynamic warm-ups increase muscle elasticity and joint synovial fluid, while a clean, dry sprung floor prevents ankle sprains and falls.

B. Energy

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Energy
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Energy governs how movement happens, distinguishing between percussive, sustained, swinging, suspended, or collapsing movement qualities (p. 10).

quiz_item.question: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
options: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
choices: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Enamel protects the crown over dentin and the central neurovascular pulp while cementum covers the root; cariogenic bacteria in plaque metabolize dietary carbohydrates into acids that dissolve tooth enamel unless removed by brushing, flossing, and fluoride protection.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
quiz_item.question: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
options: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
choices: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Handling only the crown and keeping the root moist in its socket, milk, or saline preserves living root cells for successful reimplantation by a dentist (p. 33).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
options: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
choices: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Enamel protects the crown over dentin and the central neurovascular pulp while cementum covers the root; cariogenic bacteria in plaque metabolize dietary carbohydrates into acids that dissolve tooth enamel unless removed by brushing, flossing, and fluoride protection.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
options: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
choices: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Handling only the crown and keeping the root moist in its socket, milk, or saline preserves living root cells for successful reimplantation by a dentist (p. 33).

C. To harden soft dental stone impressions in the mouth

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To dye invisible bacterial plaque so patients can see missed spots
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Disclosing dye colors nearly invisible plaque deposits on teeth, showing patients exactly where to improve their brushing and flossing technique (p. 31).

options: A. To heat the plaster so it sets in under ten seconds
B. To bring trapped air bubbles to the surface so the stone cast has no pits
C. To polish the metal impression tray before sterilization
D. To separate the water from the powder after mixing
choices: A. To heat the plaster so it sets in under ten seconds
B. To bring trapped air bubbles to the surface so the stone cast has no pits
C. To polish the metal impression tray before sterilization
D. To separate the water from the powder after mixing
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. To bring trapped air bubbles to the surface so the stone cast has no pits
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Gentle mechanical vibration flows the stone mixture into every tooth indentation while driving out air bubbles that would leave holes in the finished cast (p. 29).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does fluoride work together with saliva to protect teeth that have already erupted into the mouth?
options: A. It coats the teeth in a permanent waterproof plastic layer
B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
C. It numbs the nerve endings inside the pulp chamber so cavities cannot hurt
D. It stops the salivary glands from secreting digestive enzymes
choices: A. It coats the teeth in a permanent waterproof plastic layer

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Topical fluoride attracts minerals from saliva back into microscopic areas of acid-weakened enamel, reversing the earliest stages of decay (p. 33).

C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
choices: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Lossless compression reduces file size while preserving 100 percent of the original data, which is essential for text, spreadsheets, and executable programs where missing bytes would corrupt the file (p. 26).

requirements.lead_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor.
requirements.req_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor. (a) Using a spreadsheet or database program, develop a food budget for a patrol weekend campout OR create a troop roster that includes the name, rank, patrol, and telephone number of each Scout. Show your counselor that you can sort the roster by each of the following categories: rank, patrol, and alphabetically by name. (b) Using a word processor, write a draft letter inviting the parents or guardians of your troop's Scouts to a troop event. Resource: Word Processing Tutorial (video) (c) Using a graphics program, design and draw a campsite plan for your troop OR create a flyer for an upcoming troop event, incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (d) Using a presentation software program, develop a report about a topic approved by your counselor. For your presentation, create at least five slides, with each one incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (e) Using a digital device, take a picture of a troop activity. Send or transfer this image to a device where it can be shared with your counselor. (f) Make a digital recording of your voice, transfer the file to a different device, and have your counselor play back the recording. pamphlet_excerpts: Organizing Information With Databases: Database manager (DBM) programs are used for organizing, storing, and keeping track of a set of information called a database (p. 49).
Database Records and Fields: The data are organized in lines called records, with each record consisting of a number of fields (p. 49).
Uniform Field Structure Across Records: For each new record, the same set of fields is stored, with different contents in each field (p. 49).
Troop Attendance Database Design: A troop attendance database could be set up with a record for each Scout in the troop (p. 49).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Define Standard Database Fields: For each new record, the same set of fields is stored, with different contents in each field (p. 49).
Step 2 - Create Individual Scout Records: A troop attendance database could be set up with a record for each Scout in the troop (p. 49).
Step 3 - Add Patrol and Rank Columns: Each record would consist of fields for the Scout's name, patrol, rank, troop meeting attendance, campout attendance, and other events (p. 49).
Step 4 - Log Event Attendance Status: An entry of "present" or "absent" could be made in the appropriate field of each Scout's record after each activity (p. 49).

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Describe why it is important to properly dispose of digital technology. (b) Explain to your counselor why it is important to use a certified recycler of digital technology hardware or devices. Share what you learned with your counselor. (e) Find a battery recycling center near you and find out what it does to recycle batteries. Share what you have learned with your counselor about the proper methods for recycling batteries.

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to the Digital Technology merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Under the BSA Digital Safety guidelines in Digital Technology Requirement 1, what is the safest way to protect your accounts and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) online?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Under the BSA Digital Safety guidelines in Digital Technology Requirement 1, what is the safest way to protect your accounts and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) online?
options: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it, and accept friend requests from unknown adults.

B. Use long, unique passphrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
C. Disable firewall and operating system security updates because patches slow down video streaming and gaming.
D. Click on urgent pop-up links claiming your account is suspended and enter your credentials on the linked form immediately.
choices: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it, and accept friend requests from unknown adults.

B. Use long, unique passphrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
C. Disable firewall and operating system security updates because patches slow down video streaming and gaming.
D. Click on urgent pop-up links claiming your account is suspended and enter your credentials on the linked form immediately.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Use long, unique passphrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Digital Technology Requirement 1 emphasizes safeguarding PII, using strong unique passphrases with multi-factor authentication, keeping software updated, avoiding phishing links, and following BSA Youth Protection digital rules.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How did the availability of the VisiCalc spreadsheet program change business computing in the late 1970s and early 1980s?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How did the availability of the VisiCalc spreadsheet program change business computing in the late 1970s and early 1980s?
options: A. It forced small companies to rent time on government mainframes
B. It sparked a trend of companies installing personal computers in the workplace
C. It eliminated the need for operating systems like MS-DOS
D. It raised the price of desktop computers above $50,000
choices: A. It forced small companies to rent time on government mainframes
B. It sparked a trend of companies installing personal computers in the workplace
C. It eliminated the need for operating systems like MS-DOS
D. It raised the price of desktop computers above $50,000
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It sparked a trend of companies installing personal computers in the workplace
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Because VisiCalc was not available on mainframe systems, it helped start a major trend of companies adopting personal computers in the workplace (p. 23).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why would a software engineer choose lossless compression instead of lossy compression when archiving a financial spreadsheet or software program?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why would a software engineer choose lossless compression instead of lossy compression when archiving a financial spreadsheet or software program?
options: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
choices: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Lossless compression reduces file size while preserving 100 percent of the original data, which is essential for text, spreadsheets, and executable programs where missing bytes would corrupt the file (p. 26).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does spyware typically behave once it gets onto a computer or mobile device?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does spyware typically behave once it gets onto a computer or mobile device?
options: A. It organizes troop attendance records into fields and rows
B. It speeds up the CPU clock rate to improve gaming graphics
C. It tracks your movements on the web and can install secret programs
D. It encrypts your web browser connections using HTTPS
choices: A. It organizes troop attendance records into fields and rows
B. It speeds up the CPU clock rate to improve gaming graphics
C. It tracks your movements on the web and can install secret programs
D. It encrypts your web browser connections using HTTPS
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. It tracks your movements on the web and can install secret programs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Spyware is malicious software, often bundled with useful programs, that secretly tracks a user's web browsing and can install additional hidden programs (p. 49).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the key difference between a web address starting with HTTP and one starting with HTTPS?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the key difference between a web address starting with HTTP and one starting with HTTPS?
options: A. HTTP is reserved for government computers, while HTTPS is for schools
B. HTTP sends data as plain text, while HTTPS encrypts the communication
C. HTTPS disables images so web pages load faster on dial-up
D. HTTP requires a security certificate padlock, while HTTPS does not
choices: A. HTTP is reserved for government computers, while HTTPS is for schools
B. HTTP sends data as plain text, while HTTPS encrypts the communication
C. HTTPS disables images so web pages load faster on dial-up
D. HTTP requires a security certificate padlock, while HTTPS does not
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. HTTP sends data as plain text, while HTTPS encrypts the communication
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): HTTP exchanges data in unencrypted plain text, whereas HTTPS encrypts the data sent between your browser and the server to protect logins and personal information (p. 59).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In a troop attendance database, what is the line of information for a single Scout called, and what are the individual categories like Name, Patrol, and Rank called?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In a troop attendance database, what is the line of information for a single Scout called, and what are the individual categories like Name, Patrol, and Rank called?
options: A. The Scout's line is a browser, and the categories are protocols
B. The Scout's line is a field, and the categories are records
C. The Scout's line is a record, and the categories are fields
D. The Scout's line is a pixel, and the categories are vectors
choices: A. The Scout's line is a browser, and the categories are protocols
B. The Scout's line is a field, and the categories are records
C. The Scout's line is a record, and the categories are fields
D. The Scout's line is a pixel, and the categories are vectors
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The Scout's line is a record, and the categories are fields
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Database manager programs organize each item on a line called a record, with each record divided into consistent categories called fields (p. 49).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the legal term for making or trading unauthorized copies of copyrighted software, music, or movies?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the legal term for making or trading unauthorized copies of copyrighted software, music, or movies?
options: A. Lossless compression
B. Open-source licensing
C. Piracy
D. Trademark registration
choices: A. Lossless compression
B. Open-source licensing
C. Piracy
D. Trademark registration
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Piracy
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Copyright law prohibits making unauthorized copies of protected works, and trading in illegal copies is called piracy (p. 80).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the EPA, besides keeping toxic chemicals out of landfills, what is a major benefit of recycling one million cell phones?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the EPA, besides keeping toxic chemicals out of landfills, what is a major benefit of recycling one million cell phones?
options: A. It generates enough electricity to power a mainframe computer for a year
B. It recovers thousands of pounds of copper along with hundreds of pounds of silver and gold
C. It automatically erases all spyware from the internet
D. It converts old lithium batteries into fiber-optic cables
choices: A. It generates enough electricity to power a mainframe computer for a year
B. It recovers thousands of pounds of copper along with hundreds of pounds of silver and gold
C. It automatically erases all spyware from the internet
D. It converts old lithium batteries into fiber-optic cables
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It recovers thousands of pounds of copper along with hundreds of pounds of silver and gold
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The EPA reports that recycling one million cell phones recovers 35,000 pounds of copper, 772 pounds of silver, 75 pounds of gold, and 33 pounds of palladium (p. 73).

pamphlet_excerpts: Focusing on Personal Abilities: Many people with disabilities want to emphasize what they are able to do rather than emphasize their disabilities (p. 9).
Recognizing the Person First: Remember that people with disabilities are people first (p. 9).
Respecting Individual Self-Description: Each person gets to decide how he or she should be described (p. 9).
Applying Person-First Language: You should use person-first language when talking about people who are not personal acquaintances or about people with disabilities as agroup (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Honor Personal Description Choices: Each person gets to decide how he or she should be described (p. 9).
Step 2 - Use Person-First Language: You should use person-first language when talking about people who are not personal acquaintances or about people with disabilities as agroup (p. 9).
Step 3 - Ask New Friends Directly: When you make a new friend or talk about an individual, show a person-first attitude by calling the individual what he orshe wants to be called (p. 9).
Step 4 - Acknowledge Whole Personal Identity: Many people with disabilities see their condition as part ofwho they are, just like their gender, hair or eye color, or ethnicity (p. 9).

options: A. Speak only to the person's companion or interpreter in a loud voice, and assume anyone who does not use a wheelchair has no disability.
B. Push a person's wheelchair or grab a blind person's white cane without asking so you can move them through doorways faster.

D. Avoid inviting Scouts with physical or sensory disabilities on campouts so the troop does not have to adjust trail plans.

Foundational High School Courses: In school, take biology, physical science, language, and physical education classes (p. 19).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Volunteer With Support Agencies: Get an after-schooljob or volunteer with an agency or organization that serves people who have disabilities (p. 19).

Step 3 - Measure Hearing With Audiometers: An audiologist uses an instrument called anaudiometer to test a person's hearing (p. 19).

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following options: (a) Option A, Access. Visit TWO of the following locations and take notes about the accessibility to people with disabilities. Discuss your observations with your counselor. Visit TWO of the following locations and take notes while observing features and methods that are used to accommodate people with invisible disabilities. While there, ask staff members to explain any accommodation features that may not be obvious. Note anything you think could be done to better accommodate people who have invisible disabilities. pamphlet_excerpts: Tailored Individual Accommodations: An accommodation is just a different way of doing things that is tailored to the individual needs of a person with a disability (p. 36).
Classroom Learning Accommodations: Most schools are accommodating students with disabilities to make learning better (p. 36).
Workplace and Attraction Supports: Accommodations also happen in workplaces to make work easier and in public attractions to make experiences more enjoyable (p. 36).
Evaluating and Improving Accommodations: For requirement 4b, you are to identify accommodations that already exist at certain places and suggest better accommodations (p. 36).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Workplace Supports: Accommodations also happen in workplaces to make work easier and in public attractions to make experiences more enjoyable (p. 36).
Step 2 - Document Existing Facility Accommodations: For requirement 4b, you are to identify accommodations that already exist at certain places and suggest better accommodations (p. 36).

Step 3 - Interview On-Site Staff Members: You will need to talk with staff members at the locations or facilities to help you understand the accommodations, because they often are not obvious (p. 36).
Step 4 - Inspect Public Site Usability: Next time you are in a public place, look at how accessible (usable) the location is for people with disabilities (p. 36).

requirements.lead_text: Explain what advocacy is. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Explain what advocacy is. Do ONE of the following: (a) Present a counselor-approved disabilities awareness program to a Cub Scout pack or other group. During your presentation, explain and use person-first language. (b) Find out about disabilities awareness education programs in your school or school system, or contact a disability advocacy agency. Volunteer with a program or agency for eight hours. (c) Using resources such as disability advocacy agencies, government agencies, the internet (with your parent or guardian's permission), and news magazines, learn about myths and misconceptions that influence the general public's understanding of people with disabilities. List 10 myths and misconceptions about people with disabilities and learn the facts about each myth. Share your list with your counselor, then use it to make a presentation to a Cub Scout pack or other group.

pamphlet_excerpts: Harm of Mistaken Stereotypes: We are all hurt by mistaken ideas and misunderstandings about people with disabilities and what they can and cannotdo (p. 19).
Sharing Accurate Factual Information: Learn the facts so you can share the correct information with others (p. 19).
Disability Versus Illness Distinction: Having a disability is not the same as being sick (p. 19).
Health and Athletic Strength: Many people with disabilities are in excellent physical condition, healthy, athletic, and strong (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Separate Disability From Illness: Having a disability is not the same as being sick (p. 19).
Step 2 - Recognize Physical Fitness: Many people with disabilities are in excellent physical condition, healthy, athletic, and strong (p. 19).
Step 3 - Distinguish Temporary Medical Conditions: Some people who have disabilities also have illnesses, just as some nondisabled people are ill (p. 19).
Step 4 - Refute Quality-of-Life Myths: A person with a disability has a poor quality of life or lives a life totally different from people without disabilities (p. 19).

pamphlet_excerpts: Core Meaning of Advocacy: Advocacy, Attitudes, and Awareness Advocacy means supporting, promoting, encouraging, or defending something (p. 44).
Promoting Positive Community Attitudes: To be an advocate for people with disabilities means you support and encourage positive attitudes about people with disabilities (p. 44).
Courage to Challenge Mistreatment: It can also mean that you are brave enough to challenge false and unfair beliefs or call to account those who mistreat people with disabilities (p. 44).
Removing Stereotypical Labels: You help strip away the labels so that people can see each other as individuals (p. 44).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Challenge Unfair Beliefs Bravely: It can also mean that you are brave enough to challenge false and unfair beliefs or call to account those who mistreat people with disabilities (p. 44).
Step 2 - Look Past Stereotypical Labels: You help strip away the labels so that people can see each other as individuals (p. 44).
Step 3 - Build Mutual Respect Daily: You help build bridges of understanding and respect among all people, regardless of their abilities (p. 44).
Step 4 - Teach Awareness to Others: In completing the requirements for the Disabilities Awareness merit badge, you have learned things that you can now teach to others (p. 44).

Step 3 - Classify Breeds by Function: In the late 1800s, at the same time that dog shows we regaining popularity, a system was developed for classifying breeds according to how they are used (p. 12).
Step 4 - Review AKC Registry Standards: In the United States, the American Kennel Club has maintained a registry of breeds since 1884 (p. 12).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
quiz_item.question: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
options: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
choices: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Stiff muscles, pinned ears, tucked tail, showing the whites of the eyes ('whale eye'), yawning/lip-licking under tension, and growling are clear canine warning signs of fear or defensiveness.

Frequent Short Training Sessions: Multiple, short periods of training are most effective (p. 37).

Step 3 - Extend Adult Dog Sessions: Older dogs can tolerate sessions of up to 20 minutes long (p. 37).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Where on a dog's body should you place your fingers to check its pulse?
quiz_item.question: Where on a dog's body should you place your fingers to check its pulse?
options: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
B. On the tip of the muzzle right behind the nose pad
C. At the base of the tail on the top of the spine
D. Under the front paw pads between the toes
choices: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
B. On the tip of the muzzle right behind the nose pad
C. At the base of the tail on the top of the spine

quiz_item.correct_answer: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The femoral artery runs close to the skin on the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh near the belly, making it the best spot to feel a dog's pulse (p. 55).

pamphlet_excerpts: Miacis Early Carnivore Ancestor: The origin of dogs can be traced to an animal called Miacis, which looked more like a weasel than a dog (p. 9).
Prehistoric Carnivore Physical Traits: This small, flesh-eating creature had short legs, a long tail, five toes, and teeth like those of today's carnivores (p. 9).
Cynodictis Canine Dentition Traits: The next important ancestor, called Cynodictis was the first to have doglikecharacteristics, such as a shortened fifth toe, 42 teeth, and longer legs (p. 9).
Tomarctus Modern Dog Resemblance: Then came a descendent of Cynodictis, called Tomarctus, which resembled today's dogs even (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trace Early Canine Dentition: The next important ancestor, called Cynodictis was the first to have doglikecharacteristics, such as a shortened fifth toe, 42 teeth, and longer legs (p. 9).
Step 2 - Compare Tomarctus Physical Features: Then came a descendent of Cynodictis, called Tomarctus, which resembled today's dogs even (p. 9).
Step 3 - Identify Evolved Dewclaw Anatomy: This animal had short, erect ears, long legs and tail, and adewclaw that had developed from the shortened fifth toe (p. 9).
Step 4 - Observe Modern Canine Instincts: Also, Tomarctus probably behaved much like today's dogs (p. 9).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
options: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
choices: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Stiff muscles, pinned ears, tucked tail, showing the whites of the eyes ('whale eye'), yawning/lip-licking under tension, and growling are clear canine warning signs of fear or defensiveness.

options: A. Small and medium dogs live about 15 years, while large dogs typically live nine to 12 years
B. Large dogs live 18 to 20 years, while small dogs average eight to 10 years
C. All dog breeds share the same 12-year average lifespan regardless of body size
D. Medium dogs live half as long as giant working breeds
choices: A. Small and medium dogs live about 15 years, while large dogs typically live nine to 12 years
B. Large dogs live 18 to 20 years, while small dogs average eight to 10 years
C. All dog breeds share the same 12-year average lifespan regardless of body size
D. Medium dogs live half as long as giant working breeds
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Small and medium dogs live about 15 years, while large dogs typically live nine to 12 years
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Body size strongly affects canine longevity: small and medium dogs live around 15 years, whereas large dogs generally live nine to 12 years (p. 27).

B. Teaching the dog complex police apprehension and scent-detection routines
C. Helping your dog fit in safely and happily with your family and society

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): While some dogs learn specialized service or police work, the fundamental goal of training your pet is helping it fit in safely with you, your family's activities, and the broader community (p. 35).

B. Dry kibble is fortified with medicine while canned food is only for treats
C. Canned food is mostly water, even though it is more flavorful
D. Dogs cannot digest cooked meat in canned formulas
choices: A. Canned food contains no protein or fat
B. Dry kibble is fortified with medicine while canned food is only for treats

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Canned food is mostly water, even though it is more flavorful

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What training schedule works best when teaching basic obedience commands to a puppy?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What training schedule works best when teaching basic obedience commands to a puppy?
options: A. One 60-minute session every Saturday morning
B. Two 45-minute drills each day before meals
C. Continuous training for two hours until the puppy masters every command
D. Four or five short sessions a day lasting five to 10 minutes each
choices: A. One 60-minute session every Saturday morning
B. Two 45-minute drills each day before meals
C. Continuous training for two hours until the puppy masters every command
D. Four or five short sessions a day lasting five to 10 minutes each
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Four or five short sessions a day lasting five to 10 minutes each
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Puppies have short attention spans, so four or five brief sessions per day of five to 10 minutes each are most effective, while older dogs can handle up to 20 minutes (p. 37).

options: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
B. On the tip of the muzzle right behind the nose pad
C. At the base of the tail on the top of the spine
D. Under the front paw pads between the toes
choices: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
B. On the tip of the muzzle right behind the nose pad
C. At the base of the tail on the top of the spine
D. Under the front paw pads between the toes
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The femoral artery runs close to the skin on the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh near the belly, making it the best spot to feel a dog's pulse (p. 55).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: How are heartworms and tapeworms transmitted to dogs?
options: A. Both are spread directly through coughing at dog parks
B. Heartworms are spread by mosquito bites, while tapeworms are spread by fleas
C. Heartworms come from drinking puddle water, while tapeworms come from ticks
D. Both are inherited only from an infected mother before birth
choices: A. Both are spread directly through coughing at dog parks
B. Heartworms are spread by mosquito bites, while tapeworms are spread by fleas
C. Heartworms come from drinking puddle water, while tapeworms come from ticks
D. Both are inherited only from an infected mother before birth
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Heartworms are spread by mosquito bites, while tapeworms are spread by fleas
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dogs contract heartworms from the bite of an infected mosquito, while tapeworms are transmitted when a dog swallows an infected flea (p. 57).

options: A. Miacis

choices: A. Miacis

B. Cushioning the impact of running and muffling noise

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A dog's paw pads act as shock absorbers to cushion the impact of running while also muffling footsteps as the dog moves (p. 30).

options: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.

requirements.req_text: Using the formatted sheet of paper you prepared for your manual project, produce a pencil drawing as it would be used for manufacturing. Fill in all title block information. The manual drawing may be any one of the following drawing types: (a) Architectural: Make a scale drawing of an architectural project. The architectural drawing may be a floor plan; electrical, plumbing, or mechanical service plan; elevation plan; or landscaping plan. Use an architect's scale and show dimensions to communicate the actual size of features. Include any important sectional drawings, notes, and considerations necessary for construction. Properly print a bill of materials for at least three of the raw materials or components in the project. (b) Mechanical: Make a scale drawing of some mechanical device or interesting object. The mechanical drawing may be of the orthographic (third-angle) or isometric style. Use an engineer's scale and show dimensions to communicate the actual size of features. Include any important sectional drawings, notes, and manufacturing considerations. Properly print a bill of materials for at least three of the raw materials or components in the assembly. (c) Electrical: Draw a simple schematic of a radio or electronic circuit. Properly print a bill of materials including all of the major electrical components used in the circuit. Use standard drawing symbols to represent the electronic components.

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a facility or industry workplace where drafting is part of the business. Ask to see an example of the work that is done there, the different drafting facilities, and the tools used. (1) Find out how much of the drafting done there is manual and how much is done using CAD. If CAD is used, find out what software is used and how and why it was chosen. (2) Ask about the drafting services provided. Ask who uses the designs produced in the drafting area and how those designs are used. Discuss how the professionals who perform drafting cooperate with other individuals in the drafting area and other areas of the business. (3) Ask how important the role of drafting is to producing the end product or service that this business supplies. Find out how drafting contributes to the company's end product or service. (b) Using resources you find on your own such as at the library and on the internet (with your parent or guardian's permission), learn more about the drafting trade and discuss the following with your counselor. (1) The drafting tools used in the past, why and how they were used. Explain which tools are still used today and how their use has changed with the advent of new tools. Discuss which tools are being made obsolete by newer tools in the industry. (2) Tell what media types were used in the past and how drawings were used, stored, and reproduced. Tell how the advent of CAD has changed the media used, and discuss how these changes affect the storage or reproduction of drawings. (3) Discuss whether the types of media have changed such that there are new uses the drawings, or other outputs, produced by designers. Briefly discuss how new media types are used in the industry today.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Drafting Requirement 1, how does third-angle orthographic projection represent a three-dimensional object on a flat drawing sheet, and how are object lines distinguished from hidden lines?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Drafting Requirement 1, how does third-angle orthographic projection represent a three-dimensional object on a flat drawing sheet, and how are object lines distinguished from hidden lines?
options: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.

D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
choices: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.

D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Orthographic projection aligns multiple 2D views (typically front, top, and right side) to convey exact geometry to scale, using a standardized alphabet of lines where visible edges are thick solid lines and hidden edges are dashed.

options: A. Because each single view shows all three dimensions at once

D. Because each view gives only two-dimensional information and shares dimensions with adjacent views
choices: A. Because each single view shows all three dimensions at once

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Because each view gives only two-dimensional information and shares dimensions with adjacent views

requirements.req_text: Demonstrate that you know how to respond to electrical emergencies by doing the following: (a) Explain how to turn off power for a particular circuit and the whole house in the event of an emergency. (d) Show how to render first aid to a person who is unconscious from an apparent electrical shock. (e) Show how to treat an electrical burn. (f) Explain what to do in the event of an electrical fire. (g) Explain what to do if caught out in the open during an electrical storm.

quiz_item.question: You discover a person in contact with a damaged, live 120-volt extension cord who is unable to let go due to muscular tetany. According to Electricity Requirement 1, what must you do first?
options: A. Grab the victim's bare shoulders with both hands and pull them briskly away from the wire before calling 911.

B. Do not touch the victim with bare hands; immediately disconnect the power source by shutting off the main circuit breaker or unplugging the cord (or use a dry, nonconductive wooden pole if power cannot be shut off), then call 911 and check for breathing.
C. Throw a bucket of tap water over the extension cord to cool the sparks and extinguish the electrical arc.
D. Use a metal pry bar to lift the live copper wire off the person's hand while standing on a damp garage floor.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why is it important to check for outlets that have loose-fitting plugs during your home electrical safety inspection?
quiz_item.question: Why is it important to check for outlets that have loose-fitting plugs during your home electrical safety inspection?
options: A. Loose plugs reduce the voltage frequency from 60 hertz to 30 hertz
B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
C. Loose plugs cause the household electric meter to spin backward
D. Loose-fitting plugs convert alternating current into direct current
choices: A. Loose plugs reduce the voltage frequency from 60 hertz to 30 hertz
B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
C. Loose plugs cause the household electric meter to spin backward
D. Loose-fitting plugs convert alternating current into direct current
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Outlets with loose-fitting plugs create resistance and arcing at the contact points, which can overheat and lead to a fire (p. 51).

B. The homeowner must tap the push button dozens of times per second
C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
D. The metal gong repels the iron striker as soon as they touch
choices: A. The battery rapidly reverses its positive and negative terminals

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): When the electromagnet pulls the striker toward the gong, the armature breaks contact with the interrupter screw, shutting off the magnetism so the spring pulls the armature back to repeat the cycle (p. 49).

Worn Insulation Short Circuits: Insulation wears off and the bare wires short-circuit (p. 48).
Warning Signs of Shorts: A flash of light and a smell of burning insulation indicate a short circuit (p. 48).
Low Resistance Current Surge: Since the current suddenly encounters lower resistance, more current transfers, and that blows a fuse or trips the circuit breaker (p. 48).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Watch for Short Circuit Signs: A flash of light and a smell of burning insulation indicate a short circuit (p. 48).
Step 2 - Prevent Low-Resistance Current Surges: Since the current suddenly encounters lower resistance, more current transfers, and that blows a fuse or trips the circuit breaker (p. 48).
Step 3 - Push Breaker Handle Off: Some circuit breakers used in homes are the push-push type; others have a handle that must be pushed to the offposition before the breaker (p. 48).
Step 4 - Follow Panel Reset Instructions: Follow the instructions on your home's circuit breaker panel to properly reset whatever type (p. 48).

options: A. Both lamps go out immediately because the single loop is broken
B. The remaining lamp stays lit because parallel branches provide independent paths for current
C. The battery short-circuits and melts the switch
D. The remaining lamp flickers at 60 cycles per second
choices: A. Both lamps go out immediately because the single loop is broken
B. The remaining lamp stays lit because parallel branches provide independent paths for current
C. The battery short-circuits and melts the switch
D. The remaining lamp flickers at 60 cycles per second
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. The remaining lamp stays lit because parallel branches provide independent paths for current
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In a parallel circuit, each lamp has its own branch path connected across the battery, so removing one bulb does not interrupt current to the other bulb (p. 49).
