pamphlet_excerpts: Charged Particle Beams: Particle accelerators, sometimes called atom smashers, are machines that can create beams of electrically charged particles and accelerate them (p. 23).
Increasing Kinetic Energy: This acceleration increases the particles' energy of motion (p. 23).
Fastball Energy Analogy: Think of the difference between catching a baseball that is gently underhanded to you and catching a fast ball fired at youby a major-league pitcher (p. 23).
Energy Binding Matter: Energy is the universal container that holds things together (p. 23).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Compare Low and High Energy: Think of the difference between catching a baseball that is gently underhanded to you and catching a fast ball fired at youby a major-league pitcher (p. 23).
Step 2 - Recognize Nuclear Binding Energy: Energy is the universal container that holds things together (p. 23).
Step 3 - Overcome Atomic Container Energy: If you want to break open a container such as an atom or a proton to see what's inside, you must overcome that container'senergy (p. 23).
Step 4 - Probe Subatomic Particle Makeup: From accelerators, scientists get the energy they need to break open and explore the makeup of atomic and subatomic particles (p. 23).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why do physicists need particle accelerators to study the internal makeup of atomic nuclei and nucleons?
quiz_item.question: Why do physicists need particle accelerators to study the internal makeup of atomic nuclei and nucleons?
options: A. Accelerators freeze atoms to absolute zero so their electrons stop moving
B. Accelerators magnify visible light waves enough to photograph individual quarks directly
C. High-energy particle beams are needed to overcome the strong binding energy holding nuclei and nucleons together
D. Only uncharged neutrons can be pushed by static electricity in a vacuum tube
choices: A. Accelerators freeze atoms to absolute zero so their electrons stop moving
B. Accelerators magnify visible light waves enough to photograph individual quarks directly
C. High-energy particle beams are needed to overcome the strong binding energy holding nuclei and nucleons together
D. Only uncharged neutrons can be pushed by static electricity in a vacuum tube
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. High-energy particle beams are needed to overcome the strong binding energy holding nuclei and nucleons together
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Energy holds atoms and nucleons together like a container, and particle accelerators give charged particles enough kinetic energy to break open and probe those subatomic structures (p. 23).

requirements.lead_text: Radiation Safety. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Radiation Safety. Do ONE of the following: (a) Using a radiation survey meter and a radioactive source, show how the counts per minute change as the source gets closer to or farther from the radiation detector. Adults must handle radioactive materials. Place three different materials between the source and the detector, then explain any differences in the measurements per minute. Explain how time, distance, and shielding can reduce an individual's radiation dose. (b) Describe how radon is detected in homes. Discuss the steps taken for the long-term and short-term test methods, tell how to interpret the results, and explain when each type of test should be used. Explain the health concerns related to radon gas and tell what steps can be taken to reduce radon in buildings. (c) Visit a place where X-rays are used. Draw a floor plan of this room. Show where the unit, the unit operator, and the patient would be when the X-ray unit is operated. Explain the precautions taken and the importance of those precautions for the safety of the operator.

pamphlet_excerpts: Radiation in Scientific Research: Nuclear Technologies Radiation in Science The uses of radiation in science and research are many and varied (p. 42).
Carbon-14 in Living Things: All living things have some radioactive carbon-14 in them (p. 42).
Archaeological Radiocarbon Dating: Archaeologists and paleontologists use this measurement in their studies (p. 42).

Step 3 - Deploy Alpha Particle Spectrometers: The Mars rover Sojourner used alpha particles to identify chemical elements in Martian rocks (p. 42).
Step 4 - Read Induced Martian X-Rays: An instrument on the rover bombarded selected rocks with alpha particles, then read the X-rays generated from the rocks (p. 42).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Under the ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) radiation safety principle, what are the three primary methods used to minimize exposure to ionizing radiation?
options: A. Ventilation, grounding, and magnetic deflection.
B. Filtration, chemical neutralization, and thermal cooling.
C. Compression, humidification, and ultraviolet sterilization.
D. Minimizing time spent near the source, maximizing distance from the source, and placing appropriate shielding between yourself and the source.
choices: A. Ventilation, grounding, and magnetic deflection.
B. Filtration, chemical neutralization, and thermal cooling.
C. Compression, humidification, and ultraviolet sterilization.
D. Minimizing time spent near the source, maximizing distance from the source, and placing appropriate shielding between yourself and the source.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Minimizing time spent near the source, maximizing distance from the source, and placing appropriate shielding between yourself and the source.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Radiation protection relies on Time, Distance, and Shielding: reducing exposure duration, increasing distance (which follows the inverse-square law), and using proper absorber materials.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. They each have one proton, but they have zero, one, and two neutrons respectively
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Ordinary hydrogen has 1 proton and 0 neutrons, deuterium has 1 proton and 1 neutron, and radioactive tritium has 1 proton and 2 neutrons (p. 12).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do physicists need particle accelerators to study the internal makeup of atomic nuclei and nucleons?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do physicists need particle accelerators to study the internal makeup of atomic nuclei and nucleons?
options: A. Accelerators freeze atoms to absolute zero so their electrons stop moving
B. Accelerators magnify visible light waves enough to photograph individual quarks directly
C. High-energy particle beams are needed to overcome the strong binding energy holding nuclei and nucleons together
D. Only uncharged neutrons can be pushed by static electricity in a vacuum tube
choices: A. Accelerators freeze atoms to absolute zero so their electrons stop moving
B. Accelerators magnify visible light waves enough to photograph individual quarks directly
C. High-energy particle beams are needed to overcome the strong binding energy holding nuclei and nucleons together
D. Only uncharged neutrons can be pushed by static electricity in a vacuum tube
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. High-energy particle beams are needed to overcome the strong binding energy holding nuclei and nucleons together
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Energy holds atoms and nucleons together like a container, and particle accelerators give charged particles enough kinetic energy to break open and probe those subatomic structures (p. 23).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: In a cloud chamber experiment using dry ice and methanol, what safety precautions and physical principles apply?
options: A. Seal the dry ice in an airtight glass jar and heat the methanol over an open flame
B. Store dry ice in a vented cooler, wear gloves in a well-ventilated area when handling poisonous and flammable methanol, and watch vapor trails condense along ionized particle paths
C. Drink a small amount of methanol to test its purity and handle radioactive sources barehanded without an adult
D. Submerge the dry ice in boiling water so alpha particles float to the surface
choices: A. Seal the dry ice in an airtight glass jar and heat the methanol over an open flame
B. Store dry ice in a vented cooler, wear gloves in a well-ventilated area when handling poisonous and flammable methanol, and watch vapor trails condense along ionized particle paths
C. Drink a small amount of methanol to test its purity and handle radioactive sources barehanded without an adult
D. Submerge the dry ice in boiling water so alpha particles float to the surface
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Store dry ice in a vented cooler, wear gloves in a well-ventilated area when handling poisonous and flammable methanol, and watch vapor trails condense along ionized particle paths
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dry ice must be stored in a cooler that vents subliming CO2 gas, methanol must be handled with gloves in a ventilated area because it is flammable and poisonous, and an adult must handle any radioactive source (p. 33).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: What key discovery by Lise Meitner, Otto Hahn, Fritz Strassmann, and Enrico Fermi made sustained nuclear energy production possible?
options: A. Striking uranium with a slow neutron splits the nucleus in half and releases additional neutrons that can sustain a controlled chain reaction
B. Heating ordinary hydrogen gas with a candle causes it to fuse into solid lead
C. Fast neutrons bounce off uranium nuclei without ever splitting them unless the uranium is frozen
D. Control rods speed up neutrons so every atom in the reactor splits at the exact same microsecond
choices: A. Striking uranium with a slow neutron splits the nucleus in half and releases additional neutrons that can sustain a controlled chain reaction
B. Heating ordinary hydrogen gas with a candle causes it to fuse into solid lead
C. Fast neutrons bounce off uranium nuclei without ever splitting them unless the uranium is frozen

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Striking uranium with a slow neutron splits the nucleus in half and releases additional neutrons that can sustain a controlled chain reaction
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Meitner concluded that a neutron hits and splits the uranium nucleus (fission), and Fermi showed that slowing down the released neutrons allows a self-sustaining chain reaction (p. 53).

pamphlet_excerpts: Atmospheric Carbon Cycle Role: The Oceans and the Atmosphere We still have a lot to learn about the role of oceans in the atmospheric carbon cycle (p. 32).
Warm Pacific Current Flow: El Niño (ehl NEEN yoh) is a warm current in the Pacific Ocean that flows southward along South America'swest coast (p. 32).
El Niño Return Cycle: It usually lasts nine to 12 months and returns on average every four years (p. 32).
Severe Global Weather Impacts: A powerful El Niño in 1982 and 1983 caused severe drought in Australia and Indonesia and an unusually large number of storms in California (p. 32).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Track Four Year Cycles: It usually lasts nine to 12 months and returns on average every four years (p. 32).
Step 2 - Assess Regional Weather Extremes: A powerful El Niño in 1982 and 1983 caused severe drought in Australia and Indonesia and an unusually large number of storms in California (p. 32).
Step 3 - Compare Historical Event Severity: More recent El Niño events in 2003 and 2006 were not as devastating (p. 32).
Step 4 - Identify Tropical Wind Shifts: Scientists believe El Niño is related to a shift in air movements over the tropical Pacific Ocean (p. 32).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How do marine phytoplankton and the global ocean interact with Earth's atmosphere to support life and regulate climate?
quiz_item.question: How do marine phytoplankton and the global ocean interact with Earth's atmosphere to support life and regulate climate?
options: A. Deep-sea hydrothermal vents produce most atmospheric oxygen, while surface currents reflect all incoming solar heat back into space.
B. Marine phytoplankton generate at least half of Earth's atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis, while ocean waters absorb vast amounts of solar heat and carbon dioxide.
C. Saltwater evaporation removes carbon dioxide from the ocean and locks it permanently into stratospheric clouds.
D. Ocean tides generate geothermal heat that warms polar air masses without transferring moisture to the atmosphere.
choices: A. Deep-sea hydrothermal vents produce most atmospheric oxygen, while surface currents reflect all incoming solar heat back into space.
B. Marine phytoplankton generate at least half of Earth's atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis, while ocean waters absorb vast amounts of solar heat and carbon dioxide.
C. Saltwater evaporation removes carbon dioxide from the ocean and locks it permanently into stratospheric clouds.
D. Ocean tides generate geothermal heat that warms polar air masses without transferring moisture to the atmosphere.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Marine phytoplankton generate at least half of Earth's atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis, while ocean waters absorb vast amounts of solar heat and carbon dioxide.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Microscopic marine phytoplankton produce over half of the world's oxygen and anchor marine food webs, while the ocean stores and redistributes solar heat and absorbs atmospheric carbon dioxide.

pamphlet_excerpts: Global Wind Circulation Systems: The Oceans and the Atmosphere Great wind circulation systems form (p. 32).
Equatorial East Trade Winds: Close to the equator, trade winds blow from the east (p. 32).
Temperate Zone Westerly Winds: In the temperate zone, steady winds called westerlies blow from the west (p. 32).
Wind Driven Surface Currents: Winds blowing across the ocean's surface create currents (p. 32).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Temperate Westerly Winds: In the temperate zone, steady winds called westerlies blow from the west (p. 32).
Step 2 - Map Wind Driven Currents: Winds blowing across the ocean's surface create currents (p. 32).
Step 3 - Trace Circular Basin Gyres: When the trade winds and westerlies blow across the oceans, they cause the currents in each ocean basin to move in acircular pattern (p. 32).
Step 4 - Analyze Global Heat Transport: Both surface and deep water currents affect the world'sclimate by moving warm air from the tropics toward the poles, and cold air (p. 32).

choices: A. They cancel each other out so that mid-ocean waters remain completely still

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. They push surface waters in opposite latitudinal bands, creating large circular current patterns
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Trade winds blowing from the east near the equator and westerlies blowing from the west in the temperate zone cause currents in each ocean basin to move in a circular pattern (p. 32).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What happens to a deep-water swell wave as it enters shallow water and forms a breaker?
quiz_item.question: What happens to a deep-water swell wave as it enters shallow water and forms a breaker?
options: A. The wave speeds up and stretches out until it flattens silently onto the sand
B. The bottom of the wave slows down from friction with the seafloor while the top pitches forward and collapses
C. Cold groundwater rises from the beach sand to push the wave back out to sea
D. Surface tension locks the wave crest in place so it cannot topple over
choices: A. The wave speeds up and stretches out until it flattens silently onto the sand
B. The bottom of the wave slows down from friction with the seafloor while the top pitches forward and collapses
C. Cold groundwater rises from the beach sand to push the wave back out to sea
D. Surface tension locks the wave crest in place so it cannot topple over
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. The bottom of the wave slows down from friction with the seafloor while the top pitches forward and collapses
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): When a wave reaches shallow water where depth is less than half its wavelength, friction with the bottom slows the wave base, increasing height and steepness until the crest pitches forward as surf (p. 27).

B. Heavy rainfall adds atmospheric salt to the sea and increases surface salinity
C. Evaporation removes dissolved sodium chloride from the ocean and makes the water fresher
D. Neither evaporation nor precipitation has any measurable effect on seawater salt content
choices: A. High evaporation removes fresh water and raises salinity, while heavy precipitation adds fresh water and lowers salinity
B. Heavy rainfall adds atmospheric salt to the sea and increases surface salinity

quiz_item.correct_answer: A. High evaporation removes fresh water and raises salinity, while heavy precipitation adds fresh water and lowers salinity

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Make a plankton net. Tow the net by a dock, wade with it, hold it in a current, or tow it from a rowboat. Do this for about 20 minutes. Save the sample. Examine it under a microscope or high-power glass. Identify the three most common types of plankton in the sample. Note: May be done in lakes or streams. (b) Make a series of models (clay or plaster and wood) of a volcanic island. Show the growth of an atoll from a fringing reef through a barrier reef. Describe the Darwinian theory of coral reef formation. (c) Measure the water temperature at the surface, midwater, and bottom of a body of water four times daily for five consecutive days. You may measure depth with a rock tied to a line. Make a Secchi disk to measure turbidity (how much suspended sedimentation is in the water). Measure the air temperature. Note the cloud cover and roughness of the water. Show your findings (air and water temperature, turbidity) on a graph. Tell how the water temperature changes with air temperature. (d) Make a model showing the inshore sediment movement by littoral currents, tidal movement, and wave action. Include such formations as high and low waterlines, low-tide terrace, berm, and coastal cliffs. Show how offshore bars are built up and torn down. (e) Make a wave generator. Show reflection and refraction of waves. Show how groins, jetties, and breakwaters affect these patterns. (f) With your counselor's and parent or guardian's approval and permission, track and monitor satellite images available on the internet for a specific location for three weeks. Describe what you have learned to your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Diverse Marine Life Habitats: A rich assortment of living things calls the ocean home (p. 36).
Microscopic to Giant Organisms: Big and small, long and short, multicolored and drab, active and inactive, sea life ranges from microscopic plankton to the largest creatures on Earth (p. 36).
Bioluminescent Deep Sea Organisms: Some organisms even light up, like ghostly neon lights (p. 36).
Scientific Ocean Ecological Zones: The sea is so vast that scientists have divided it into zones (p. 36).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Bioluminescent Sea Life: Some organisms even light up, like ghostly neon lights (p. 36).
Step 2 - Classify Major Ocean Zones: The sea is so vast that scientists have divided it into zones (p. 36).
Step 3 - Map Open Pelagic Waters: The pelagic zone includes all the environments of the ocean above the bottom, or living in open oceans or seas rather than in waters next to land (p. 36).
Step 4 - Separate Neritic and Oceanic Zones: It is divided into an inshore neritic zone (the zone of shallow water adjoining the seacoast) and the open-sea oceanic zone (p. 36).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How do marine scientists divide the pelagic zone of the ocean?
quiz_item.question: How do marine scientists divide the pelagic zone of the ocean?
options: A. Into the inshore neritic zone adjoining the seacoast and the open-sea oceanic zone
B. Into the freshwater river zone and the underground aquifer zone
C. Into the trade wind zone and the westerly wind belt
D. Into the guyot peak zone and the basaltic rock basin
choices: A. Into the inshore neritic zone adjoining the seacoast and the open-sea oceanic zone
B. Into the freshwater river zone and the underground aquifer zone
C. Into the trade wind zone and the westerly wind belt
D. Into the guyot peak zone and the basaltic rock basin
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Into the inshore neritic zone adjoining the seacoast and the open-sea oceanic zone
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The pelagic zone encompasses all ocean water environments above the seafloor and is divided into the shallow inshore neritic zone and the open-sea oceanic zone (p. 36).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do marine phytoplankton and the global ocean interact with Earth's atmosphere to support life and regulate climate?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do marine phytoplankton and the global ocean interact with Earth's atmosphere to support life and regulate climate?
options: A. Deep-sea hydrothermal vents produce most atmospheric oxygen, while surface currents reflect all incoming solar heat back into space.
B. Marine phytoplankton generate at least half of Earth's atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis, while ocean waters absorb vast amounts of solar heat and carbon dioxide.
C. Saltwater evaporation removes carbon dioxide from the ocean and locks it permanently into stratospheric clouds.
D. Ocean tides generate geothermal heat that warms polar air masses without transferring moisture to the atmosphere.
choices: A. Deep-sea hydrothermal vents produce most atmospheric oxygen, while surface currents reflect all incoming solar heat back into space.
B. Marine phytoplankton generate at least half of Earth's atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis, while ocean waters absorb vast amounts of solar heat and carbon dioxide.
C. Saltwater evaporation removes carbon dioxide from the ocean and locks it permanently into stratospheric clouds.
D. Ocean tides generate geothermal heat that warms polar air masses without transferring moisture to the atmosphere.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Marine phytoplankton generate at least half of Earth's atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis, while ocean waters absorb vast amounts of solar heat and carbon dioxide.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Microscopic marine phytoplankton produce over half of the world's oxygen and anchor marine food webs, while the ocean stores and redistributes solar heat and absorbs atmospheric carbon dioxide.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do the trade winds and westerlies work together to shape surface circulation in each ocean basin?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do the trade winds and westerlies work together to shape surface circulation in each ocean basin?
options: A. They cancel each other out so that mid-ocean waters remain completely still
B. They push surface waters in opposite latitudinal bands, creating large circular current patterns
C. They force all ocean water to flow exclusively from the poles straight to the equator
D. They heat the ocean floor directly to generate vertical volcanic plumes
choices: A. They cancel each other out so that mid-ocean waters remain completely still
B. They push surface waters in opposite latitudinal bands, creating large circular current patterns
C. They force all ocean water to flow exclusively from the poles straight to the equator
D. They heat the ocean floor directly to generate vertical volcanic plumes
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. They push surface waters in opposite latitudinal bands, creating large circular current patterns
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Trade winds blowing from the east near the equator and westerlies blowing from the west in the temperate zone cause currents in each ocean basin to move in a circular pattern (p. 32).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens to a deep-water swell wave as it enters shallow water and forms a breaker?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens to a deep-water swell wave as it enters shallow water and forms a breaker?
options: A. The wave speeds up and stretches out until it flattens silently onto the sand
B. The bottom of the wave slows down from friction with the seafloor while the top pitches forward and collapses
C. Cold groundwater rises from the beach sand to push the wave back out to sea
D. Surface tension locks the wave crest in place so it cannot topple over
choices: A. The wave speeds up and stretches out until it flattens silently onto the sand
B. The bottom of the wave slows down from friction with the seafloor while the top pitches forward and collapses
C. Cold groundwater rises from the beach sand to push the wave back out to sea
D. Surface tension locks the wave crest in place so it cannot topple over
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. The bottom of the wave slows down from friction with the seafloor while the top pitches forward and collapses
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): When a wave reaches shallow water where depth is less than half its wavelength, friction with the bottom slows the wave base, increasing height and steepness until the crest pitches forward as surf (p. 27).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How did submerged flat-topped undersea mountains known as guyots get their shape?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How did submerged flat-topped undersea mountains known as guyots get their shape?
options: A. Heavy deep-sea currents scraped the tops off underwater sand dunes
B. Submarines and dredging vessels leveled the peaks for navigation safety
C. Wave action eroded and flattened exposed volcanic seamount peaks during lower Ice Age sea levels
D. Tectonic plates pulled the mountain summits apart into wide rift valleys
choices: A. Heavy deep-sea currents scraped the tops off underwater sand dunes
B. Submarines and dredging vessels leveled the peaks for navigation safety
C. Wave action eroded and flattened exposed volcanic seamount peaks during lower Ice Age sea levels
D. Tectonic plates pulled the mountain summits apart into wide rift valleys
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Wave action eroded and flattened exposed volcanic seamount peaks during lower Ice Age sea levels
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): During the last Ice Age, lower sea levels exposed volcanic seamount peaks to surface wave action that eroded and flattened their tops before melting glaciers submerged them again as guyots (p. 14).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do differences in evaporation and precipitation affect the salinity of surface ocean water?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do differences in evaporation and precipitation affect the salinity of surface ocean water?
options: A. High evaporation removes fresh water and raises salinity, while heavy precipitation adds fresh water and lowers salinity
B. Heavy rainfall adds atmospheric salt to the sea and increases surface salinity
C. Evaporation removes dissolved sodium chloride from the ocean and makes the water fresher
D. Neither evaporation nor precipitation has any measurable effect on seawater salt content
choices: A. High evaporation removes fresh water and raises salinity, while heavy precipitation adds fresh water and lowers salinity
B. Heavy rainfall adds atmospheric salt to the sea and increases surface salinity
C. Evaporation removes dissolved sodium chloride from the ocean and makes the water fresher
D. Neither evaporation nor precipitation has any measurable effect on seawater salt content
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. High evaporation removes fresh water and raises salinity, while heavy precipitation adds fresh water and lowers salinity
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Evaporation leaves salts behind in the sea and increases salinity, whereas precipitation dilutes seawater with fresh rain or snow and lowers salinity (p. 31).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which group of marine organisms consists of microscopic plants and animals that drift with ocean currents and form the base of ocean food chains?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which group of marine organisms consists of microscopic plants and animals that drift with ocean currents and form the base of ocean food chains?
options: A. Benthos
B. Nekton
C. Holdfast seaweeds
D. Plankton
choices: A. Benthos
B. Nekton
C. Holdfast seaweeds
D. Plankton
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Plankton
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Plankton, from the Greek word for wanderer, includes microscopic drifting plants (phytoplankton) and animals (zooplankton) that form the basis of all major ocean food chains (p. 45).

options: A. Winds slow down the rotation of ocean basins during the afternoon
B. High tide occurs regularly every 12 hours and 25 minutes, following the moon's orbit as Earth rotates
C. Internal waves block tidal water from reaching the beach until sunset
D. Groins and jetties delay the arrival of tidal water by several hours
choices: A. Winds slow down the rotation of ocean basins during the afternoon
B. High tide occurs regularly every 12 hours and 25 minutes, following the moon's orbit as Earth rotates
C. Internal waves block tidal water from reaching the beach until sunset
D. Groins and jetties delay the arrival of tidal water by several hours
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. High tide occurs regularly every 12 hours and 25 minutes, following the moon's orbit as Earth rotates
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): On most ocean shores, high tide occurs regularly every 12 hours and 25 minutes, which means each new high or low tide occurs a little later each day (p. 23).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When taking a bearing from a topographic map in an area with a 12-degree west magnetic declination, why must you account for declination before following your compass in the field?
quiz_item.question: When taking a bearing from a topographic map in an area with a 12-degree west magnetic declination, why must you account for declination before following your compass in the field?
options: A. Because contour lines on a topographic map shift position seasonally as soil moisture changes.
B. Because a baseplate compass needle always points toward the geographic North Pole rather than magnetic north.
C. Because map grid lines align with true north while the compass needle points to magnetic north, and ignoring a 12-degree difference will pull you far off course over distance.
D. Because metal control flags placed at orienteering checkpoints reverse the polarity of the compass housing.
choices: A. Because contour lines on a topographic map shift position seasonally as soil moisture changes.
B. Because a baseplate compass needle always points toward the geographic North Pole rather than magnetic north.
C. Because map grid lines align with true north while the compass needle points to magnetic north, and ignoring a 12-degree difference will pull you far off course over distance.
D. Because metal control flags placed at orienteering checkpoints reverse the polarity of the compass housing.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Because map grid lines align with true north while the compass needle points to magnetic north, and ignoring a 12-degree difference will pull you far off course over distance.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Magnetic declination is the angular difference between true north (shown on the map) and magnetic north (where the compass needle points); failing to adjust for it causes significant navigation errors.

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Convert Map Compass Angles: If the magnetic north-south lines are not drawn on the map, convert the language of the compass to that of the map (p. 10).

Step 3 - Read Exact Degree Bearings: The bearing is 244 degrees from "A" to "B." (Points "A" and "B" can be seen in the top photo on page 21.) (p. 10).
Step 4 - Navigate With Thumb Compasses: The thumb compass rides on the thumb and simplifies map orientation and direction finding while you are on the move (p. 10).

pamphlet_excerpts: Adjusting for Speed Changes: Every timeorienteers switch from walking to running or the reverse, they must mentally adjust the pace and time as well (p. 26).
Counting Paces and Time: Once you have laid out the course, start at the beginning and walk the length of it, counting the number of paces and recording the time it takes you to reach (p. 26).
Baseline Per Hundred Meters: This is your walking pace and time per 100 meters (p. 26).
Averaging Multiple Pace Trials: You will get a more accurate measure if you walk the course two or more times and then divide the total paces and minutes by the total meters walked (p. 26).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Record Hundred Meter Baseline: This is your walking pace and time per 100 meters (p. 26).
Step 2 - Average Multiple Course Runs: You will get a more accurate measure if you walk the course two or more times and then divide the total paces and minutes by the total meters walked (p. 26).
Step 3 - Account for Uneven Ground: This is particularly important if the course is on uneven ground (p. 26).
Step 4 - Measure Running Pace Speed: Judging Distance on the Ground Running Pace/Time Foot speed is important in orienteering, especially for competitiveorienteering (p. 26).

common_misconception_pair.fact: If you aim straight at a control on a linear feature and miss it slightly, you will not know which way to turn, whereas aiming off deliberately to one side tells you the exact direction to turn (p. 38).

pamphlet_excerpts: Turning at Linear Features: If you arrive at the linear feature and do not see the control, you will then know which way to turn to find (p. 38).
Avoiding Direction Uncertainty: In this map, it would be easy to reach the road and not be sure what direction the control lies (p. 38).
Deliberate Aiming Off Strategy: To prevent this, you can deliberately aim a few meters south of the control so you know to turn north when you get to the road (p. 38).
Mental Picture of Terrain: Keep a clear mental picture of the terrain that you will pass through (p. 38).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Aim Off to One Side: To prevent this, you can deliberately aim a few meters south of the control so you know to turn north when you get to the road (p. 38).
Step 2 - Visualize Upcoming Terrain Shapes: Keep a clear mental picture of the terrain that you will pass through (p. 38).
Step 3 - Read Map Every Few Seconds: Read the map every few seconds, think beyond your location, and plan ahead (p. 38).
Step 4 - Plan Ahead After Controls: The best way to practice reading ahead is to take time at the beginning of the course and after each control to make sure you understand (p. 38).

quiz_item.question: Why would an orienteer deliberately aim a few meters south of a control located along a north-south road?
options: A. To compensate for a broken compass bezel during the race
B. To guarantee that upon reaching the road, they know to turn north to find the control
C. To avoid having to punch the control card at that station
D. To add extra distance so their pace count reaches an even number
choices: A. To compensate for a broken compass bezel during the race
B. To guarantee that upon reaching the road, they know to turn north to find the control
C. To avoid having to punch the control card at that station
D. To add extra distance so their pace count reaches an even number
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. To guarantee that upon reaching the road, they know to turn north to find the control
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): This technique, called aiming off, ensures that when you hit the linear feature (the road), you know with certainty which direction to turn to reach the control (p. 38).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When taking a bearing from a topographic map in an area with a 12-degree west magnetic declination, why must you account for declination before following your compass in the field?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When taking a bearing from a topographic map in an area with a 12-degree west magnetic declination, why must you account for declination before following your compass in the field?
options: A. Because contour lines on a topographic map shift position seasonally as soil moisture changes.
B. Because a baseplate compass needle always points toward the geographic North Pole rather than magnetic north.
C. Because map grid lines align with true north while the compass needle points to magnetic north, and ignoring a 12-degree difference will pull you far off course over distance.
D. Because metal control flags placed at orienteering checkpoints reverse the polarity of the compass housing.
choices: A. Because contour lines on a topographic map shift position seasonally as soil moisture changes.
B. Because a baseplate compass needle always points toward the geographic North Pole rather than magnetic north.
C. Because map grid lines align with true north while the compass needle points to magnetic north, and ignoring a 12-degree difference will pull you far off course over distance.
D. Because metal control flags placed at orienteering checkpoints reverse the polarity of the compass housing.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Because map grid lines align with true north while the compass needle points to magnetic north, and ignoring a 12-degree difference will pull you far off course over distance.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Magnetic declination is the angular difference between true north (shown on the map) and magnetic north (where the compass needle points); failing to adjust for it causes significant navigation errors.

options: A. Add the degrees of error for west declination and subtract for east declination

C. Multiply the contour interval by the magnetic variation angle
D. Point the direction-of-travel arrow south before rotating the bezel
choices: A. Add the degrees of error for west declination and subtract for east declination

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Add the degrees of error for west declination and subtract for east declination
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): To convert from true north on the map to magnetic north on the compass, always add the degrees of error for west declination and subtract for east declination (p. 10).

pamphlet_excerpts: Understanding Paint Sheen: Sheen is a critical characteristic that refers to the degree of shine or gloss of any coating or surface (p. 43).
Existing Sheen Impact: The sheen currently on the surface can determine the amount of surface preparation required (p. 43).
Durability and Appearance: The abrasion resistance, chemical resistance, and overall beauty of the painted area (p. 43).
Full Sheen Spectrum: The typical full sheen range, from lowest to highest, includes flat or matte, eggshell or low luster, satin or pearl, semi gloss, and high or full gloss (p. 43).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Evaluate Durability Needs: The abrasion resistance, chemical resistance, and overall beauty of the painted area (p. 43).
Step 2 - Compare Gloss Levels: The typical full sheen range, from lowest to highest, includes flat or matte, eggshell or low luster, satin or pearl, semi gloss, and high or full gloss (p. 43).
Step 3 - Check Manufacturer Standards: Because there are no industry wide standard definitions of these terms, gloss levels may vary from one manufacturer to another (p. 43).
Step 4 - Match Sheen to Surface: The type of sheen you choose will depend on what you are painting (p. 43).

pamphlet_excerpts: Primer as Final Prep: Applying primer, the first coat of paint, also is the last stage of surface preparation (p. 51).
Bonding and Sealing Functions: The primer makes the next coat stick to the surface, protects the substrate, and seals the surface (p. 51).
Substrate-Specific Primers: There are different primers for wood, concrete and masonry, plaster and drywall, steel, and other metals (p. 51).
Indoor and Outdoor Wood Primers: Wood primers are available in oil-based or water-based products and can be used indoors or outdoors (p. 51).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Select Substrate Primer: There are different primers for wood, concrete and masonry, plaster and drywall, steel, and other metals (p. 51).
Step 2 - Prime Bare Wood Surfaces: Wood primers are available in oil-based or water-based products and can be used indoors or outdoors (p. 51).
Step 3 - Apply Alkali-Resistant Masonry Primer: Exterior masonry surfaces are often highly alkaline, so be sure to use primers on surfaces that are alkali-resistant (p. 51).
Step 4 - Remove Loose Plaster Dust: Make sure primers for plaster surfaces are alkali-resistant and that plaster dust is removed first (p. 51).

pamphlet_excerpts: Immediate Tool Cleaning: Care and Storage of Equipment The most important part of taking care of any paint application tool or equipment is cleaning it immediately (p. 54).
Avoiding Costly Tool Damage: Failure to do so can cost you more time and more money spent on special cleaners, which in some cases may ruin the tool (p. 54).
Extending Brush Lifespan: If you clean your brushes after each use, they will last along time (p. 54).
Saving Time and Money: Cleaning takes only a few minutes and saves hours of work and, quite possibly, the cost of replacement (p. 54).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Wash Brushes Immediately: If you clean your brushes after each use, they will last along time (p. 54).
Step 2 - Rinse Out Wet Paint: Cleaning takes only a few minutes and saves hours of work and, quite possibly, the cost of replacement (p. 54).
Step 3 - Prevent Hardened Bristles: If paint is allowed to harden in a brush, cleaning that brush becomes adifficult and time-consuming task, one that could have been easily avoided (p. 54).
Step 4 - Wrap Overnight in Foil: If the same brush and paint have been used over several days, store the brush for the night (with most of the paint wiped off) in tightly folded aluminum (p. 54).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How can you temporarily store a brush overnight when using the same paint across several consecutive days?
quiz_item.question: How can you temporarily store a brush overnight when using the same paint across several consecutive days?
options: A. Stand the wet brush upright on its bristles inside an empty bucket.
B. Place the uncovered brush outside in direct sunlight so the surface skin hardens.
C. Wipe off most of the excess paint and wrap the bristles tightly in folded aluminum foil.
D. Boil the bristles in hot water for ten minutes before leaving it on the workbench.
choices: A. Stand the wet brush upright on its bristles inside an empty bucket.
B. Place the uncovered brush outside in direct sunlight so the surface skin hardens.
C. Wipe off most of the excess paint and wrap the bristles tightly in folded aluminum foil.
D. Boil the bristles in hot water for ten minutes before leaving it on the workbench.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Wipe off most of the excess paint and wrap the bristles tightly in folded aluminum foil.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): When pausing overnight on a multi-day project with the same coating, wiping off excess paint and wrapping the brush tightly in aluminum foil keeps air out so the paint does not harden (p. 54).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When setting up an extension ladder to scrape, prime, and paint an exterior wall, how should you position the base of the ladder according to the 4-to-1 rule?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When setting up an extension ladder to scrape, prime, and paint an exterior wall, how should you position the base of the ladder according to the 4-to-1 rule?
options: A. Place the base of the ladder 1 foot away from the wall for every 4 feet of vertical height to the upper support point, on firm level ground.
B. Place the base 4 feet away from the wall for every 1 foot of vertical height so you can lean backward while rolling paint.
C. Set the ladder rails flush against the siding and tie the top rung to a rain gutter with twine.
D. Extend the ladder to its maximum length with zero overlap between sections and prop one leg on loose bricks.
choices: A. Place the base of the ladder 1 foot away from the wall for every 4 feet of vertical height to the upper support point, on firm level ground.
B. Place the base 4 feet away from the wall for every 1 foot of vertical height so you can lean backward while rolling paint.
C. Set the ladder rails flush against the siding and tie the top rung to a rain gutter with twine.
D. Extend the ladder to its maximum length with zero overlap between sections and prop one leg on loose bricks.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Place the base of the ladder 1 foot away from the wall for every 4 feet of vertical height to the upper support point, on firm level ground.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The 4-to-1 ladder safety rule places the base 1 foot out from the wall for every 4 feet of working height, providing a stable 75-degree climbing angle that prevents tipping backward or sliding out.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which sequence correctly lists the typical paint sheen range from the lowest shine to the highest gloss?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which sequence correctly lists the typical paint sheen range from the lowest shine to the highest gloss?
options: A. Flat, eggshell, satin, semi-gloss, and high gloss
B. Eggshell, flat, pearl, high gloss, and semi-gloss
C. Satin, matte, low luster, full gloss, and semi-gloss
D. Matte, semi-gloss, eggshell, satin, and full gloss
choices: A. Flat, eggshell, satin, semi-gloss, and high gloss
B. Eggshell, flat, pearl, high gloss, and semi-gloss
C. Satin, matte, low luster, full gloss, and semi-gloss
D. Matte, semi-gloss, eggshell, satin, and full gloss
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Flat, eggshell, satin, semi-gloss, and high gloss
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The standard sheen spectrum progresses from flat or matte at the lowest shine up through eggshell, satin, semi-gloss, and high or full gloss (p. 43).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why must you choose a specialized primer when preparing exterior masonry or plaster surfaces for painting?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why must you choose a specialized primer when preparing exterior masonry or plaster surfaces for painting?
options: A. Masonry and plaster surfaces are completely nonporous and reject water-based coatings.
B. Standard wood primers dry too slowly when exposed to concrete and brick.
C. Masonry primers eliminate the need to patch cracks or apply a topcoat.
D. Exterior masonry and plaster are often highly alkaline, requiring an alkali-resistant primer after dust removal.
choices: A. Masonry and plaster surfaces are completely nonporous and reject water-based coatings.
B. Standard wood primers dry too slowly when exposed to concrete and brick.
C. Masonry primers eliminate the need to patch cracks or apply a topcoat.
D. Exterior masonry and plaster are often highly alkaline, requiring an alkali-resistant primer after dust removal.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Exterior masonry and plaster are often highly alkaline, requiring an alkali-resistant primer after dust removal.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Masonry and plaster contain alkaline compounds that degrade ordinary primers, so painters must remove surface dust and apply an alkali-resistant primer (p. 51).

B. Six primary colors and six secondary colors arranged by brightness
C. Three primary colors (red, yellow, blue), three secondary colors (green, orange, purple), and six intermediate colors

choices: A. Four primary colors, four neutral grays, and four pastel tints

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Three primary colors (red, yellow, blue), three secondary colors (green, orange, purple), and six intermediate colors
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The basic 12-color wheel combines three primary colors (red, yellow, blue), three secondary colors (green, orange, purple), and six intermediate or tertiary colors positioned between them (p. 31).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: How can you temporarily store a brush overnight when using the same paint across several consecutive days?
options: A. Stand the wet brush upright on its bristles inside an empty bucket.
B. Place the uncovered brush outside in direct sunlight so the surface skin hardens.
C. Wipe off most of the excess paint and wrap the bristles tightly in folded aluminum foil.
D. Boil the bristles in hot water for ten minutes before leaving it on the workbench.
choices: A. Stand the wet brush upright on its bristles inside an empty bucket.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Wipe off most of the excess paint and wrap the bristles tightly in folded aluminum foil.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): When pausing overnight on a multi-day project with the same coating, wiping off excess paint and wrapping the brush tightly in aluminum foil keeps air out so the paint does not harden (p. 54).

requirements.lead_text: Your Fitness Knowledge and Habits. Do the following with your counselor:
requirements.req_text: Your Fitness Knowledge and Habits. Do the following with your counselor: (a) Explain the physical exercise you regularly do, whether your routine includes all four components of physical fitness (cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition), and how your current practices increase or decrease your likelihood of developing cardiovascular disease or other conditions in adulthood. (b) Discuss what harmful substances you consciously avoid, and how these actions affect your risk factors now and in the future. (c) Explain what common diseases can be prevented or mitigated by vaccinations, and whether you are immunized according to the advice of your healthcare provider and the direction of your parent or guardian. (d) Discuss how good nutrition is related to the other components of personal fitness, and if you follow a nutritious, balanced diet. (e) Discuss what a healthy weight is for you, and what you do to maintain a healthy weight. (f) Explain why getting adequate sleep is important, and whether you get enough hours of sleep each night. (g) Discuss whether you spend quality time with your family and friends in social and recreational activities, and how you contribute to creating and maintaining a good home life.

options: A. Sprinting speed, vertical jump height, arm size, and calorie counting
B. Weightlifting, marathon running, vitamin supplements, and fasting
C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
D. Morning stretching, sports participation, protein shakes, and hydration

B. Weightlifting, marathon running, vitamin supplements, and fasting
C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The four essential components of physical fitness are cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition (p. 45).

requirements.lead_text: Measures of Physical Fitness. Determine with your counselor the assessments of physical fitness and nutrition you will do before, during, and after completing the 12-week program in requirement 7.
requirements.req_text: Measures of Physical Fitness. Determine with your counselor the assessments of physical fitness and nutrition you will do before, during, and after completing the 12-week program in requirement 7. (a) Include a measure of cardiorespiratory (aerobic) fitness: Record the time required to complete a mile walk or run as fast as you can. If you are unable to walk or run as a result of a disability that is permanent or is expected to last for longer than two years, work with your counselor to define a test with a similar degree of aerobic challenge. (b) Include two measures of muscular strength and endurance: Record either the number of sit-ups done in 60 seconds OR how long a plank was held; AND, record the number of either push-ups OR pull-ups done in 60 seconds. If you are unable to complete one of these exercises safely and correctly, work with your counselor to replace it with a different exercise that measures strength and endurance. (c) Include at least one measure of flexibility, such as a back-saver sit-and-reach test or a back scratch test.

requirements.lead_text: Plan the Program. Outline with your counselor a comprehensive 12-week physical fitness and nutrition program that you will complete based on your improvement goals and ability. The program must incorporate the following:
requirements.req_text: Plan the Program. Outline with your counselor a comprehensive 12-week physical fitness and nutrition program that you will complete based on your improvement goals and ability. The program must incorporate the following: (a) Warm-up: low-intensity movement or gentle muscle stretching before each more rigorous workout (b) Cardiorespiratory (aerobic) element: an activity that raises your heart and respiratory rate for 15 to 30 minutes at least three times per week (c) Muscular strength and endurance element: repetitive exercises that target different muscles, upper body, core, and/or legs, based on your improvement goals and potential (d) Flexibility element: movements that arch/lower/stretch/relax your back, rotate your trunk, or stretch your hamstrings (e) Cool-down: low-intensity movement or gentle stretching to prevent muscle cramps and enhance the benefits of exercise (f) A plan for achieving your two improvement goals related to diet and nutrition

pamphlet_excerpts: Applying the FITT Principle: To improve cardio respiratory fitness, think of the FITT idea from page 46 (p. 69).
Aerobic Frequency and Intensity: The goal for any type of aerobic exercise is to have a Frequency of 3 to 5 days per week, an Intensity of 5-8 on a 10 point scale, and a Time (p. 69).
Alternating Vigorous and Slow Pace: Start your program by using a plan that alternates periods of vigorous and slow/resting activity (p. 69).
Building Toward Thirty Minutes: Do what you can without exhausting yourself, even if it's only 5 minutes, and work up to completing a 30-minute session (p. 69).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Alternate Vigorous and Rest Periods: Start your program by using a plan that alternates periods of vigorous and slow/resting activity (p. 69).
Step 2 - Build Duration Without Exhaustion: Do what you can without exhausting yourself, even if it's only 5 minutes, and work up to completing a 30-minute session (p. 69).
Step 3 - Progress Steadily Each Workout: With each workout you will find yourself getting more fit (p. 69).
Step 4 - Reach Thirty Minutes Continuous Jogging: Over time, you will find you can jog the entire 30 minutes (p. 69).

B. Alternate periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity and gradually build up to 30 minutes
C. Skip aerobic exercise completely and only perform sit-ups and push-ups
D. Exercise once every two weeks for two hours at maximum intensity

requirements.lead_text: Complete the Program. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Complete the Program. Do the following: (a) Complete and keep a log, over 12 consecutive weeks, of the physical fitness and nutrition program you have outlined. (If your program is interrupted by illness or unavoidable conflicts for less than two weeks, you may resume where you left off, adding the missed days or weeks at the end.) (b) During week 4 and week 8 of your program, repeat the assessments you did in requirement 5(a) before you began. Repeat the same tests for a final assessment within two weeks after completing the 12-week program. Show improvement over your pre-assessment results. (c) For three days during week 8, and again during week 12, keep a log of what you eat and drink. Show improvement toward the diet and nutrition goals you set in requirement 5(d). (d) Discuss your results, improvements, insights, and experiences with your counselor after completing the program and assessments.

pamphlet_excerpts: Exploring Personal Fitness Careers: There are many exciting careers in the field of personal fitness (p. 84).
Personal Trainer Business Policies: Personal trainers should have written policies explaining their services, costs, cancellations, length of contract, and emergency procedures (p. 84).
Exercise Physiologist Evaluations: Exercise physiologists also evaluate cardiovascular and metabolic effects in people, and help active athletes improve and maintain (p. 84).
Workplaces Hiring Fitness Professionals: Colleges and universities, rehabilitation clinics, hospitals, sports and athletic programs, and health/fitness facilities hire exercise physiologists (p. 84).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Evaluate Cardiovascular Exercise Effects: Exercise physiologists also evaluate cardiovascular and metabolic effects in people, and help active athletes improve and maintain (p. 84).

Step 2 - Explore Clinical and Athletic Employers: Colleges and universities, rehabilitation clinics, hospitals, sports and athletic programs, and health/fitness facilities hire exercise physiologists (p. 84).
Step 3 - Maintain First Aid Certifications: They should hold first-aid and CPR certifications (p. 84).
Step 4 - Assist Mobility Through Physical Therapy: People who have trouble moving or performing everyday activities need the help of a physical therapist (p. 84).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before beginning the 12-week Personal Fitness training program, why is a medical physical examination and dental checkup required along with baseline fitness testing?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before beginning the 12-week Personal Fitness training program, why is a medical physical examination and dental checkup required along with baseline fitness testing?
options: A. To exempt Scouts from flexibility and cardiorespiratory testing if they already play a varsity school sport.
B. To calculate maximum one-rep weightlifting loads so you can skip warm-up sets during week one.
C. To replace daily nutrition tracking with a prescription vitamin regimen.
D. To identify any underlying health conditions or physical limitations that need attention before strenuous exercise and to establish safe, individualized health habits.
choices: A. To exempt Scouts from flexibility and cardiorespiratory testing if they already play a varsity school sport.
B. To calculate maximum one-rep weightlifting loads so you can skip warm-up sets during week one.
C. To replace daily nutrition tracking with a prescription vitamin regimen.
D. To identify any underlying health conditions or physical limitations that need attention before strenuous exercise and to establish safe, individualized health habits.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To identify any underlying health conditions or physical limitations that need attention before strenuous exercise and to establish safe, individualized health habits.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A preventive medical evaluation ensures it is safe to perform vigorous cardiorespiratory and muscular testing and helps tailor the 12-week personal fitness plan to your health needs.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the recommended first step before beginning any new personal fitness program?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the recommended first step before beginning any new personal fitness program?
options: A. Purchasing expensive weightlifting shoes and a gym membership
B. Getting a physical examination from your doctor using the Annual Health and Medical Record form
C. Running a timed five-mile race to test your maximum heart rate
D. Eliminating all carbohydrates and fats from your daily meals
choices: A. Purchasing expensive weightlifting shoes and a gym membership
B. Getting a physical examination from your doctor using the Annual Health and Medical Record form
C. Running a timed five-mile race to test your maximum heart rate
D. Eliminating all carbohydrates and fats from your daily meals
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Getting a physical examination from your doctor using the Annual Health and Medical Record form
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Before starting a personal fitness program, you should get a physical examination from your doctor and document it on the Annual Health and Medical Record form (p. 13).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which four components must be included to achieve complete physical fitness?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which four components must be included to achieve complete physical fitness?
options: A. Sprinting speed, vertical jump height, arm size, and calorie counting
B. Weightlifting, marathon running, vitamin supplements, and fasting
C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
D. Morning stretching, sports participation, protein shakes, and hydration
choices: A. Sprinting speed, vertical jump height, arm size, and calorie counting
B. Weightlifting, marathon running, vitamin supplements, and fasting
C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
D. Morning stretching, sports participation, protein shakes, and hydration
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The four essential components of physical fitness are cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition (p. 45).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do you compare your initial physical fitness test scores to the percentile tables in the pamphlet?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do you compare your initial physical fitness test scores to the percentile tables in the pamphlet?
options: A. To see if you are allowed to start the 12-week exercise log
B. To rank Scouts in your troop from most athletic to least athletic
C. To replace the final fitness test at the end of week 12
D. To identify your current fitness baseline and prioritize areas needing improvement
choices: A. To see if you are allowed to start the 12-week exercise log
B. To rank Scouts in your troop from most athletic to least athletic
C. To replace the final fitness test at the end of week 12
D. To identify your current fitness baseline and prioritize areas needing improvement
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To identify your current fitness baseline and prioritize areas needing improvement
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Comparing your assessment scores to the reference tables helps you understand your current fitness level and identify areas at or below the 20th percentile that need extra focus (p. 65).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before using weights or specialized exercise equipment in your fitness routine, what precaution must you take?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before using weights or specialized exercise equipment in your fitness routine, what precaution must you take?
options: A. Get instruction on the safe use of the equipment from a qualified coach or instructor
B. Test the heaviest weight available to find your one-repetition maximum
C. Complete at least eight weeks of running before touching any equipment
D. Only use the equipment when you are exercising alone at home
choices: A. Get instruction on the safe use of the equipment from a qualified coach or instructor
B. Test the heaviest weight available to find your one-repetition maximum
C. Complete at least eight weeks of running before touching any equipment
D. Only use the equipment when you are exercising alone at home
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Get instruction on the safe use of the equipment from a qualified coach or instructor
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): To prevent injury, you must never attempt to use weights or special exercise equipment without first getting instruction on safe use from a coach or instructor (p. 74).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the FITT guidelines in the pamphlet, how should you start an aerobic program if you cannot yet jog for 30 minutes continuously?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the FITT guidelines in the pamphlet, how should you start an aerobic program if you cannot yet jog for 30 minutes continuously?
options: A. Push yourself to exhaustion on day one until you finish 30 minutes
B. Alternate periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity and gradually build up to 30 minutes
C. Skip aerobic exercise completely and only perform sit-ups and push-ups
D. Exercise once every two weeks for two hours at maximum intensity
choices: A. Push yourself to exhaustion on day one until you finish 30 minutes
B. Alternate periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity and gradually build up to 30 minutes
C. Skip aerobic exercise completely and only perform sit-ups and push-ups
D. Exercise once every two weeks for two hours at maximum intensity
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Alternate periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity and gradually build up to 30 minutes
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): You should start by alternating periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity without exhausting yourself, gradually working up to a 30-minute session (p. 69).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When must you repeat your physical fitness assessments and three-day nutrition logs during the 12-week program?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When must you repeat your physical fitness assessments and three-day nutrition logs during the 12-week program?
options: A. Fitness tests every single morning and nutrition logs every weekend
B. Fitness tests only in week 6 and nutrition logs only in week 10
C. Fitness assessments in weeks 4, 8, and after week 12, with three-day diet logs in weeks 8 and 12
D. Only once at the very end of week 12 right before meeting your counselor
choices: A. Fitness tests every single morning and nutrition logs every weekend
B. Fitness tests only in week 6 and nutrition logs only in week 10
C. Fitness assessments in weeks 4, 8, and after week 12, with three-day diet logs in weeks 8 and 12
D. Only once at the very end of week 12 right before meeting your counselor
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Fitness assessments in weeks 4, 8, and after week 12, with three-day diet logs in weeks 8 and 12
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): You repeat your fitness assessments in week 4, week 8, and after completing the program, while keeping three-day nutrition logs during week 8 and week 12 (p. 74).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When planning a major family purchase under Requirement 1, why should you compare total cost of ownership and financing options across multiple retailers rather than looking only at the monthly payment?
quiz_item.question: When planning a major family purchase under Requirement 1, why should you compare total cost of ownership and financing options across multiple retailers rather than looking only at the monthly payment?
options: A. Because a lower monthly payment always guarantees a lower total purchase price and zero interest charges.
B. Because long-term financing with high interest rates, fees, maintenance, and operating costs can make a low monthly payment far more expensive overall than saving up to pay cash.
C. Because retail stores are legally required to match the lowest monthly payment offered by any online auction site.
D. Because comparison shopping only applies to consumable groceries and does not affect durable goods or warranties.
choices: A. Because a lower monthly payment always guarantees a lower total purchase price and zero interest charges.
B. Because long-term financing with high interest rates, fees, maintenance, and operating costs can make a low monthly payment far more expensive overall than saving up to pay cash.
C. Because retail stores are legally required to match the lowest monthly payment offered by any online auction site.
D. Because comparison shopping only applies to consumable groceries and does not affect durable goods or warranties.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Because long-term financing with high interest rates, fees, maintenance, and operating costs can make a low monthly payment far more expensive overall than saving up to pay cash.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Evaluating needs versus wants, comparison shopping for quality and price, and calculating interest, warranties, and operating expenses reveals the true total cost of a major purchase.

requirements.lead_text: Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Prepare a budget reflecting your expected income (allowance, gifts, wages), expenses, and savings for a period of 13 consecutive weeks. (b) Compare expected income with expected expenses. (1) If expenses exceed budget income, determine steps to balance your budget. (2) If income exceeds budget expenses, state how you would use the excess money (new goal, savings). (c) Track and record your actual income, expenses, and savings for 13 consecutive weeks (the same 13-week period for which you budgeted). (You may use the forms provided in the Personal Management merit badge pamphlet, devise your own, or use a computer-generated version.) When complete, present the records showing the results to your counselor. (d) Compare your budget with your actual income and expenses to understand when your budget worked and when it did not work. With your counselor, discuss what you might do differently the next time.

Step 4 - Wait for Price Drops: The prices of many products will drop after they have been on the market (p. 14).

D. It spreads money across many different investments so poor performance in one does not ruin the whole portfolio

requirements.lead_text: Demonstrate to your counselor your understanding of time management by doing the following:
requirements.req_text: Demonstrate to your counselor your understanding of time management by doing the following: (a) Write a to-do list of tasks or activities, such as homework assignments, chores, and personal projects, that must be done in the coming week. List these in order of importance to you. (b) Make a seven-day calendar or schedule. Put in your set activities, such as school classes, sports practices or games, jobs or chores, and/or Scout or place of worship or club meetings, then plan when you will do all the tasks from your to-do list between your set activities. (c) Follow the one-week schedule you planned. Keep a daily diary or journal during each of the seven days of this week's activities, writing down when you completed each of the tasks on your to-do list compared to when you scheduled them. (d) With your counselor, review your to-do list, one-week schedule, and diary/journal to understand when your schedule worked and when it did not work. Discuss what you might do differently the next time.
