patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In ethical, customer-focused salesmanship, what is the primary goal when asking questions and listening to a prospective buyer?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In ethical, customer-focused salesmanship, what is the primary goal when asking questions and listening to a prospective buyer?
options: A. To pressure the buyer into purchasing the highest-priced item in stock regardless of whether it fits their situation.
B. To memorize a rigid script so you can talk continuously without letting the customer raise objections.
C. To understand the customer's actual needs and budget so you can honestly recommend a product or service that provides genuine value and builds long-term trust.
D. To exaggerate product performance claims during the pitch and clarify limitations only after payment is completed.
choices: A. To pressure the buyer into purchasing the highest-priced item in stock regardless of whether it fits their situation.
B. To memorize a rigid script so you can talk continuously without letting the customer raise objections.
C. To understand the customer's actual needs and budget so you can honestly recommend a product or service that provides genuine value and builds long-term trust.
D. To exaggerate product performance claims during the pitch and clarify limitations only after payment is completed.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. To understand the customer's actual needs and budget so you can honestly recommend a product or service that provides genuine value and builds long-term trust.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Successful salesmanship is built on integrity and helping the customer solve a problem by discovering their needs, presenting honest facts, and answering objections respectfully.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why does the Salesmanship merit badge pamphlet recommend visiting the factory where a product is made when practical?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why does the Salesmanship merit badge pamphlet recommend visiting the factory where a product is made when practical?
options: A. To gain firsthand knowledge of how the product is constructed so you can answer buyer questions with authority
B. To negotiate a lower personal commission rate with the assembly line workers
C. To bypass the company's marketing department and design your own packaging
D. To inspect employee attendance records before agreeing to represent the brand
choices: A. To gain firsthand knowledge of how the product is constructed so you can answer buyer questions with authority
B. To negotiate a lower personal commission rate with the assembly line workers
C. To bypass the company's marketing department and design your own packaging
D. To inspect employee attendance records before agreeing to represent the brand
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. To gain firsthand knowledge of how the product is constructed so you can answer buyer questions with authority
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Visiting the factory or business location gives a salesperson firsthand understanding of how the product is built or how the service operates (p. 12).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which elements must you examine when writing a sales plan for an assigned product and territory?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which elements must you examine when writing a sales plan for an assigned product and territory?
options: A. Only the wholesale cost of raw materials and factory shipping schedules
B. Only the personal hobbies of your merit badge counselor
C. Your target customer group, marketing channels, promotional hooks, and competitors offering similar products
D. National stock market averages from the previous ten decades
choices: A. Only the wholesale cost of raw materials and factory shipping schedules
B. Only the personal hobbies of your merit badge counselor
C. Your target customer group, marketing channels, promotional hooks, and competitors offering similar products
D. National stock market averages from the previous ten decades
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Your target customer group, marketing channels, promotional hooks, and competitors offering similar products
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Developing a strong sales plan requires writing down details about your target market, choosing marketing methods, crafting a sales hook, and analyzing competitors (p. 22).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During a sales presentation, what should you do even if you know the customer is talking to other salespeople or wants to see a proposal first?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: During a sales presentation, what should you do even if you know the customer is talking to other salespeople or wants to see a proposal first?
options: A. End the meeting immediately so you do not waste time
B. Criticize the competing salespeople by name to scare the customer
C. Refuse to provide a written proposal unless they pay a deposit first
D. Ask for the sale or order anyway after reassuring them how you can help
choices: A. End the meeting immediately so you do not waste time
B. Criticize the competing salespeople by name to scare the customer
C. Refuse to provide a written proposal unless they pay a deposit first
D. Ask for the sale or order anyway after reassuring them how you can help
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Ask for the sale or order anyway after reassuring them how you can help
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Even if the buyer wants a proposal first, is speaking to competitors, or seems undecided, you should always ask for the sale anyway (p. 26).

options: A. To buy all their inventory at full retail price from local hardware stores
B. To compare local retail prices against the bulk wholesale price the troop will pay and set a competitive price
C. To ask local store managers to stop selling fertilizer during the spring
D. To avoid keeping a written cost sheet during the fundraising campaign
choices: A. To buy all their inventory at full retail price from local hardware stores

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Comparing local retail store prices to the bulk wholesale cost allows the troop to price its product competitively while ensuring a healthy fundraising profit on the cost sheet (p. 30).

options: A. Tracking assignments in a planner, studying in a distraction-free workspace, taking structured notes in class, reviewing material regularly, and asking teachers questions early when concepts are unclear.
B. Waiting until the night before each exam to cram all chapters at once while multitasking with social media and television.
C. Copying a classmate's homework assignments verbatim so you can spend evenings re-reading the textbook cover to cover without taking notes.

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Make a list of educational places located where you live (other than schools). Visit one, and report on how you used the place for self-education. Find out how they continue to educate themselves. Discuss what you find out with your counselor. (c) Using a daily planner, show your counselor how you keep track of assignments and activities, and discuss how you manage your time. (d) Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the different methods of research available to you for school assignments, such as the library, books and periodicals, and the internet.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which study strategy best supports long-term comprehension and strong academic performance across school subjects?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which study strategy best supports long-term comprehension and strong academic performance across school subjects?
options: A. Tracking assignments in a planner, studying in a distraction-free workspace, taking structured notes in class, reviewing material regularly, and asking teachers questions early when concepts are unclear.
B. Waiting until the night before each exam to cram all chapters at once while multitasking with social media and television.
C. Copying a classmate's homework assignments verbatim so you can spend evenings re-reading the textbook cover to cover without taking notes.
D. Skipping note-taking during lectures and relying solely on memorizing boldface vocabulary words five minutes before class.
choices: A. Tracking assignments in a planner, studying in a distraction-free workspace, taking structured notes in class, reviewing material regularly, and asking teachers questions early when concepts are unclear.
B. Waiting until the night before each exam to cram all chapters at once while multitasking with social media and television.
C. Copying a classmate's homework assignments verbatim so you can spend evenings re-reading the textbook cover to cover without taking notes.
D. Skipping note-taking during lectures and relying solely on memorizing boldface vocabulary words five minutes before class.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Tracking assignments in a planner, studying in a distraction-free workspace, taking structured notes in class, reviewing material regularly, and asking teachers questions early when concepts are unclear.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Consistent daily study habits, organized note-taking, time management, academic honesty, and proactive communication with teachers produce lasting learning rather than last-minute cramming.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. By cross-referencing your subject under different but related terms to find the maximum number of useful sources
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Reference librarians are trained to cross-reference a topic across related subject terms so you can locate the widest range of books, periodicals, and digital sources (p. 41).

pamphlet_excerpts: Growing Economic Inequality: The divide between rich and poor was widening, and most families were poor or close (p. 9).
Urban Crowding and Illness: As people migrated to dirty, overcrowded cities, they were more likely to become sick and less likely to be able to enjoy nature or get physical exercise (p. 9).
Unfit Military Volunteers: In fact, when Britain went to war in 1899, more than half the men who volunteered for the army weren't fit enough to fight (p. 9).
Hardships Facing Youth: Children on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean suffered right along with their parents (p. 9).

Step 3 - Note Limited Youth Programs: Beyond the YMCA and some church-based programs, few organized activities or sports leagues were available for them to enjoy (p. 9).
Step 4 - Review Factory Child Labor: Even worse, at least 1.7 million American children under the age of 16 worked full time, sometimes working as many as 12 hours a day in factories (p. 9).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What historic event did Lord Robert Baden-Powell organize in August 1907 on Brownsea Island in Poole Harbour, England, and what did it lead to in 1908?
quiz_item.question: What historic event did Lord Robert Baden-Powell organize in August 1907 on Brownsea Island in Poole Harbour, England, and what did it lead to in 1908?
options: A. He convened the first World Scout Jamboree with 50,000 Scouts from thirty nations and founded the Order of the Arrow.
B. He wrote the United States congressional charter for the Boy Scouts of America alongside William D. Boyce and Ernest Thompson Seton.
C. He established the Philmont Scout Ranch in New Mexico and published the first American Scout Handbook.
D. He held an experimental camp with 20 boys from diverse social backgrounds organized into four patrols to test his outdoor training ideas, which led to publishing Scouting for Boys in 1908.
choices: A. He convened the first World Scout Jamboree with 50,000 Scouts from thirty nations and founded the Order of the Arrow.
B. He wrote the United States congressional charter for the Boy Scouts of America alongside William D. Boyce and Ernest Thompson Seton.
C. He established the Philmont Scout Ranch in New Mexico and published the first American Scout Handbook.
D. He held an experimental camp with 20 boys from diverse social backgrounds organized into four patrols to test his outdoor training ideas, which led to publishing Scouting for Boys in 1908.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. He held an experimental camp with 20 boys from diverse social backgrounds organized into four patrols to test his outdoor training ideas, which led to publishing Scouting for Boys in 1908.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Baden-Powell's 1907 Brownsea Island experimental camp proved the effectiveness of the Patrol Method and outdoor skills training, inspiring his 1908 publication of Scouting for Boys and the global Scouting movement.

pamphlet_excerpts: Creation of Explorer Scouts: In 1935, the BSA created a program called Explorer Scouts asone option in Senior Scouting (p. 38).
Land Alternative to Sea: It offered to older Boy Scouts a land-based alternative to Sea Scouting (p. 38).
Early Explorer Pocket Strip: Explorer Scouts initially wore the same uniform as Boy Scouts, although it featured an "Explorer Scout, BSA" strip over the right pocket (p. 38).
Forest-Green Uniforms and Posts: In the 1940s, a forest-green uniform was introduced, and Explorer Scout units began to be called posts instead of troops (p. 38).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Compare Early Uniform Strips: Explorer Scouts initially wore the same uniform as Boy Scouts, although it featured an "Explorer Scout, BSA" strip over the right pocket (p. 38).
Step 2 - Note Transition to Posts: In the 1940s, a forest-green uniform was introduced, and Explorer Scout units began to be called posts instead of troops (p. 38).
Step 3 - Identify 1944 Advancement Launch: Explorer Scouts got their own advancement program in 1944 (p. 38).
Step 4 - Review Four Explorer Ranks: The four ranks, Apprentice, Woodsman, Frontiersman, and Ranger, corresponded to the four ranks in Sea Scouting (p. 38).

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Attend either a Scouting America National Jamboree, OR World Scout Jamboree, OR a national Scouting America high-adventure base. While there, keep a journal documenting your day-to-day experiences. Upon your return, report to your counselor what you did, saw, and learned. You may include photos, brochures, and other documents in your report. (b) Write or visit the National Scouting Museum. Obtain information about this facility. Give a short report on what you think the role of this museum is in the Scouting program. (c) Visit an exhibit of Scouting memorabilia or a local museum with a Scouting history gallery, or (with your parent or guardian's permission and counselor's approval) visit with someone in your council who is recognized as a dedicated Scouting historian or memorabilia collector. Learn what you can about the history of Scouting America. Give a short report to your counselor on what you saw and learned.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: What historic event did Lord Robert Baden-Powell organize in August 1907 on Brownsea Island in Poole Harbour, England, and what did it lead to in 1908?
options: A. He convened the first World Scout Jamboree with 50,000 Scouts from thirty nations and founded the Order of the Arrow.
B. He wrote the United States congressional charter for the Boy Scouts of America alongside William D. Boyce and Ernest Thompson Seton.
C. He established the Philmont Scout Ranch in New Mexico and published the first American Scout Handbook.
D. He held an experimental camp with 20 boys from diverse social backgrounds organized into four patrols to test his outdoor training ideas, which led to publishing Scouting for Boys in 1908.
choices: A. He convened the first World Scout Jamboree with 50,000 Scouts from thirty nations and founded the Order of the Arrow.
B. He wrote the United States congressional charter for the Boy Scouts of America alongside William D. Boyce and Ernest Thompson Seton.
C. He established the Philmont Scout Ranch in New Mexico and published the first American Scout Handbook.
D. He held an experimental camp with 20 boys from diverse social backgrounds organized into four patrols to test his outdoor training ideas, which led to publishing Scouting for Boys in 1908.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. He held an experimental camp with 20 boys from diverse social backgrounds organized into four patrols to test his outdoor training ideas, which led to publishing Scouting for Boys in 1908.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Baden-Powell's 1907 Brownsea Island experimental camp proved the effectiveness of the Patrol Method and outdoor skills training, inspiring his 1908 publication of Scouting for Boys and the global Scouting movement.

pamphlet_excerpts: Causes of Diver Hyperventilation: Hyperventilation is the result of over breathing, either deliberately or because of panic (p. 21).
Dizziness and Suffocation Feelings: The likely result of hyperventilation is dizziness and fainting, and victims will feel as if they are being suffocated (p. 21).
Preparation Prevents Diving Panic: Such a condition is unlikely in diving if the participants are properly prepared for each new skill level (p. 21).
Calming a Panicked Diver: If a diver shows signs of panic at any time, bring that person back into the boat or onto shore, calm the person, and encourage slow breathing (p. 21).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Prepare Divers Before Entry: Such a condition is unlikely in diving if the participants are properly prepared for each new skill level (p. 21).
Step 2 - Bring Panicked Diver Ashore: If a diver shows signs of panic at any time, bring that person back into the boat or onto shore, calm the person, and encourage slow breathing (p. 21).
Step 3 - Provide Rest and Air: Make sure the person rests in a comfortable position and has plenty of open, fresh air (p. 21).
Step 4 - Resolve Underlying Panic Cause: Before resuming any activity, find out and resolve the cause of the panic (p. 21).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
quiz_item.question: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
options: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
choices: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Under Boyle's Law, gas volume increases as surrounding water pressure drops during ascent; holding your breath while breathing compressed air traps expanding gas in the lungs, risking life-threatening pulmonary barotrauma.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
options: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
choices: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Under Boyle's Law, gas volume increases as surrounding water pressure drops during ascent; holding your breath while breathing compressed air traps expanding gas in the lungs, risking life-threatening pulmonary barotrauma.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
quiz_item.question: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
options: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.
B. Heat vinyl modeling clays in a kitchen oven above 500 degrees Fahrenheit without ventilation to soften them.
C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
D. Hold small stone blocks between your knees while striking a cold chisel toward your body.
choices: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.
B. Heat vinyl modeling clays in a kitchen oven above 500 degrees Fahrenheit without ventilation to soften them.
C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
D. Hold small stone blocks between your knees while striking a cold chisel toward your body.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Sculpting requires eye protection against flying chips and sharp armature wires, plus wet cleanup and ventilation to avoid inhaling hazardous silica or plaster dust and solvent fumes.

requirements.lead_text: Do TWO of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Model in clay a life-size human head. Then sculpt in modeling clay, carve in wood or plaster, or use 3D modeling software to make a small-scale model of an animal or person. Explain to your counselor the method and tools you used to sculpt the figure. (b) Make a plaster mold of a fruit or vegetable. In this mold, make a copy of the fruit or vegetable. Explain to your counselor the method and tools you used to make the copy. (c) With your parent or guardian's permission and your counselor's approval, visit a museum, art exhibit, art gallery, artists' co-op, or artist's studio. After your visit, share with your counselor what you have learned. Discuss the importance of visual arts and how it strengthens social tolerance and helps stimulate cultural, intellectual, and personal development.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
options: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.
B. Heat vinyl modeling clays in a kitchen oven above 500 degrees Fahrenheit without ventilation to soften them.
C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
D. Hold small stone blocks between your knees while striking a cold chisel toward your body.
choices: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.
B. Heat vinyl modeling clays in a kitchen oven above 500 degrees Fahrenheit without ventilation to soften them.
C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
D. Hold small stone blocks between your knees while striking a cold chisel toward your body.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Sculpting requires eye protection against flying chips and sharp armature wires, plus wet cleanup and ventilation to avoid inhaling hazardous silica or plaster dust and solvent fumes.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the primary difference between modeling a figure in clay and carving a figure from a block of wood or plaster?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the primary difference between modeling a figure in clay and carving a figure from a block of wood or plaster?
options: A. Modeling is an additive process that builds up material, whereas carving is a subtractive process that removes material
B. Modeling can only be done at life-size scale, whereas carving is limited to miniature scale
C. Carving requires firing the finished piece in a kiln, whereas clay modeling never uses heat
D. Modeling requires a two-part plaster mold first, whereas carving uses 3D software exclusively
choices: A. Modeling is an additive process that builds up material, whereas carving is a subtractive process that removes material
B. Modeling can only be done at life-size scale, whereas carving is limited to miniature scale
C. Carving requires firing the finished piece in a kiln, whereas clay modeling never uses heat

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Modeling is an additive process that builds up material, whereas carving is a subtractive process that removes material
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Modeling in clay builds up a three-dimensional form by adding and shaping pliable material, while carving in wood or plaster cuts away excess material to reveal the figure (p. 23).

pamphlet_excerpts: Circulatory Failure Under Stress: The circulatory system of a person who is injured or under greats tress might not provide enough blood and oxygen to the tissues of the body (p. 43).
Deadly Untreated Shock Risks: Left untreated, it can be deadly (as organs can begin to fail) (p. 43).
Universal Shock Treatment Protocol: Treat every accident victim for shock even if no symptoms appear (p. 43).
Elevating Legs for Circulation: If you do not suspect back, neck, or head injuries, or fractures in the hip or leg, raise the feet about 12 inches to move blood from the legs to the vital (p. 43).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Treat Victims for Shock: Treat every accident victim for shock even if no symptoms appear (p. 43).

Step 2 - Elevate Uninjured Feet Safely: If you do not suspect back, neck, or head injuries, or fractures in the hip or leg, raise the feet about 12 inches to move blood from the legs to the vital (p. 43).
Step 3 - Maintain Warmth with Blankets: Keep the victim warm with blankets, coats, or sleeping bags (p. 43).
Step 4 - Avoid Harmful Snakebite Myths: Do not make any cuts on or apply suction to the bite, apply a tourniquet, or use electric shock such as from a car battery (p. 43).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Search and Rescue (SAR) operations, why is the searcher's personal safety and self-sufficiency with a prepared SAR pack considered the highest priority before entering the field?
quiz_item.question: In Search and Rescue (SAR) operations, why is the searcher's personal safety and self-sufficiency with a prepared SAR pack considered the highest priority before entering the field?
options: A. An unprepared or injured searcher becomes a second victim, diverting rescue teams and resources away from finding the original missing subject.
B. Searchers are required to hike alone off-trail without radio contact so they can cover twice as much ground.
C. Carrying the Ten Essentials allows a searcher to bypass Incident Command System (ICS) check-in at base camp.
D. Personal safety gear is only needed during night searches and can be left behind on warm summer afternoons.
choices: A. An unprepared or injured searcher becomes a second victim, diverting rescue teams and resources away from finding the original missing subject.
B. Searchers are required to hike alone off-trail without radio contact so they can cover twice as much ground.
C. Carrying the Ten Essentials allows a searcher to bypass Incident Command System (ICS) check-in at base camp.
D. Personal safety gear is only needed during night searches and can be left behind on warm summer afternoons.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. An unprepared or injured searcher becomes a second victim, diverting rescue teams and resources away from finding the original missing subject.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In SAR, responder safety comes first: checking in through the Incident Command System, working in teams, and carrying essential gear ensures rescuers do not become additional casualties.

common_misconception_pair.misconception: The Place Last Seen (PLS) and the Last Known Point (LKP) are interchangeable terms for the exact same location on a search map.
common_misconception_pair.fact: The Place Last Seen (PLS) is where an eyewitness actually saw the subject, whereas the Last Known Point (LKP) is the most recent location confirmed by physical evidence or clues such as a footprint, discarded wrapper, or cell ping (p. 64).

quiz_item.question: When planning a search for a lost school-age child, why should searchers interview the child's friends early in the investigation?

B. To learn about tracks, trails, shortcuts, and any 'secret' or favorite hideouts the child uses
C. To obtain the child's US National Grid coordinates from memory
D. To avoid having to search nearby buildings, parked vehicles, or playgrounds

requirements.lead_text: Plan and Complete a Search. Do the following with a team of Scouts, friends, or family to execute a practice SAR exercise:
requirements.req_text: Plan and Complete a Search. Do the following with a team of Scouts, friends, or family to execute a practice SAR exercise: (a) Choose a hypothetical SAR scenario, either one presented in the Search and Rescue merit badge pamphlet or one approved by your counselor. (b) Develop an Incident Action Plan (IAP) for a hasty search using the scenario information. (c) Before the search begins, conduct a PAUSE briefing to review hazards, safety concerns, personal and shared Scout Basic Essentials, and other gear. (d) Execute the search. (e) After the search, hold a team debriefing to discuss the search, problems, successful and unsuccessful tactics, and ideas for improvement.

requirements.lead_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to Search and Rescue merit badge or emergency management. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. With permission of your parent or guardian, your research methods may include an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to serve as a volunteer on a disaster relief team, a wilderness rescue team, or a ski patrol. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursue this.

Professional SAR Organization Standards: Many of these teams are members of professional organizations such as the National Association for Search and Rescue or the Mountain Rescue (p. 77).
Sheriff and State Oversight: They usually are run by local sheriff's offices or city or state agencies and may have paid positions (p. 77).
Metropolitan Police SAR Units: The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department Search and Rescue is a prime example (p. 77).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Partner with Sheriff Agencies: They usually are run by local sheriff's offices or city or state agencies and may have paid positions (p. 77).
Step 2 - Examine Police SAR Units: The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department Search and Rescue is a prime example (p. 77).
Step 3 - Explore National Park Roles: The National Park Service also employs SAR personnel throughout many national parks, most notably Denali, Grand Canyon, and Yosemite national parks (p. 77).
Step 4 - Earn Rescue Medical Credentials: Many of these national and state park positions require emergency medical, law enforcement, and fire/rescue credentials (p. 77).

options: A. An unprepared or injured searcher becomes a second victim, diverting rescue teams and resources away from finding the original missing subject.
B. Searchers are required to hike alone off-trail without radio contact so they can cover twice as much ground.
C. Carrying the Ten Essentials allows a searcher to bypass Incident Command System (ICS) check-in at base camp.
D. Personal safety gear is only needed during night searches and can be left behind on warm summer afternoons.
choices: A. An unprepared or injured searcher becomes a second victim, diverting rescue teams and resources away from finding the original missing subject.
B. Searchers are required to hike alone off-trail without radio contact so they can cover twice as much ground.
C. Carrying the Ten Essentials allows a searcher to bypass Incident Command System (ICS) check-in at base camp.
D. Personal safety gear is only needed during night searches and can be left behind on warm summer afternoons.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. An unprepared or injured searcher becomes a second victim, diverting rescue teams and resources away from finding the original missing subject.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In SAR, responder safety comes first: checking in through the Incident Command System, working in teams, and carrying essential gear ensures rescuers do not become additional casualties.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What organization receives the satellite distress signal from a registered Personal Locator Beacon (PLB) in the continental United States and coordinates with local search and rescue agencies?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What organization receives the satellite distress signal from a registered Personal Locator Beacon (PLB) in the continental United States and coordinates with local search and rescue agencies?
options: A. The National Weather Service Forecast Office
B. The Air Force Rescue Coordination Center (AFRCC)
C. The U.S. Geological Survey Topographic Division
D. The local Boy Scout Council Service Center
choices: A. The National Weather Service Forecast Office
B. The Air Force Rescue Coordination Center (AFRCC)
C. The U.S. Geological Survey Topographic Division
D. The local Boy Scout Council Service Center
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. The Air Force Rescue Coordination Center (AFRCC)
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): When activated, a Personal Locator Beacon sends a satellite distress signal to the Air Force Rescue Coordination Center (AFRCC), which verifies the alert and dispatches state or local SAR teams (p. 42).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do search and rescue teams find it easy to calculate ground distances using the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) coordinate system on a 7.5-minute USGS topographic map?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do search and rescue teams find it easy to calculate ground distances using the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) coordinate system on a 7.5-minute USGS topographic map?
options: A. UTM coordinates automatically adjust for seasonal magnetic declination shifts
B. UTM uses a metric grid system that is accurate to 1 meter
C. UTM measures elevation changes in feet rather than horizontal distance
D. UTM eliminates the need to check the map's scale or date
choices: A. UTM coordinates automatically adjust for seasonal magnetic declination shifts
B. UTM uses a metric grid system that is accurate to 1 meter
C. UTM measures elevation changes in feet rather than horizontal distance
D. UTM eliminates the need to check the map's scale or date
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. UTM uses a metric grid system that is accurate to 1 meter
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Distances are easy to calculate using the UTM grid system because it is based on meters and is accurate to 1 meter (p. 59).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In the Incident Command System (ICS), what does the concept of 'unity of command' ensure during a search and rescue operation?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In the Incident Command System (ICS), what does the concept of 'unity of command' ensure during a search and rescue operation?
options: A. Only one agency is allowed to participate in the search from start to finish
B. Every responder on the scene reports directly to the county sheriff without team leaders
C. Each person or resource reports to only one supervisor to prevent conflicting orders
D. All search teams must walk in a single unified line across the wilderness
choices: A. Only one agency is allowed to participate in the search from start to finish
B. Every responder on the scene reports directly to the county sheriff without team leaders
C. Each person or resource reports to only one supervisor to prevent conflicting orders
D. All search teams must walk in a single unified line across the wilderness
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Each person or resource reports to only one supervisor to prevent conflicting orders
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Unity of command means each person or resource responding to a scene reports to only one supervisor, which eliminates the risk of receiving conflicting orders from multiple supervisors (p. 14).

B. To prevent the dog from becoming snagged or trapped by debris

D. So the dog can swim faster through flooded basement passages
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. To prevent the dog from becoming snagged or trapped by debris
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Disaster dogs are worked off leash and without an ID vest or collar to prevent entrapment on rebar, wire, or jagged structural debris (p. 75).

intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-12-31). Sewing is using a needle and thread to make stitches and combine textiles by hand or machine. Needlework is decorative sewing and other textile arts. In this badge, you will investigate several types of sewing and needlework. You will learn basic hand and machine sewing skills and make several small, practical projects using your new skills!

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

quiz_item.question: While sewing a heavy canvas Merit Badge sash repair on a sewing machine, the needle hits a thick seam and snaps. What is the mandatory safety and machine procedure before replacing the needle?
options: A. Keep your foot on the presser-foot speed controller while reaching into the needle bar.

B. Turn off and unplug the sewing machine first, locate all broken needle fragments so none remain in the fabric, and insert a fresh heavy-duty needle with the flat shank side facing the correct direction.
C. Leave the broken needle tip inside the canvas and sew over it.
D. Hold the replacement needle between your lips while loosening the needle clamp screw with power on.
choices: A. Keep your foot on the presser-foot speed controller while reaching into the needle bar.

B. Turn off and unplug the sewing machine first, locate all broken needle fragments so none remain in the fabric, and insert a fresh heavy-duty needle with the flat shank side facing the correct direction.
C. Leave the broken needle tip inside the canvas and sew over it.
D. Hold the replacement needle between your lips while loosening the needle clamp screw with power on.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Turn off and unplug the sewing machine first, locate all broken needle fragments so none remain in the fabric, and insert a fresh heavy-duty needle with the flat shank side facing the correct direction.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Turning off power prevents accidental foot-pedal activation while fingers are near the needle bar, and recovering broken needle tips prevents puncture injuries.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When hand sewing a flat button onto a shirt or jacket, why do tailors place a toothpick or pin across the top of the button while stitching?
quiz_item.question: When hand sewing a flat button onto a shirt or jacket, why do tailors place a toothpick or pin across the top of the button while stitching?
options: A. To keep the needle from dulling against the plastic rim of the button
B. To create slack for wrapping a thread shank underneath the button
C. To measure the exact distance between the buttonholes on the placket
D. To lock the quilter's knot on the front side of the garment
choices: A. To keep the needle from dulling against the plastic rim of the button
B. To create slack for wrapping a thread shank underneath the button
C. To measure the exact distance between the buttonholes on the placket
D. To lock the quilter's knot on the front side of the garment
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. To create slack for wrapping a thread shank underneath the button
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Stitching over a pin or toothpick creates controlled slack that you wrap with thread beneath the button to form a sturdy shank, giving the buttonhole fabric space to sit flat when buttoned (p. 13).

requirements.lead_text: Choose ONE of the following options and complete each requirement:
requirements.req_text: Choose ONE of the following options and complete each requirement: (A) Machine Sewing (a) Provide a brief overview of the evolution of the sewing machine (b) Read your machine manual and do the following: (1) Explain the parts of a sewing machine and their functions. (2) Thread the machine and the bobbin. (3) Explain how to properly clean and oil the machine and change the needle. (c) Identify other tools you will need for machine sewing. Demonstrate the following sewing techniques, including when and why each is used: (1) Pinning (2) Sewing in a straight line (3) Back stitch (4) Basting stitch (5) Gathering stitch (6) Unpicking or seam ripping. (d) Do the following using a sewing machine: (1) Sew a Scout patch on your uniform or other fabric. (2) Repair a tear or small hole in fabric using a patch or darning technique. (e) Sew ONE item from this list using a pattern, using THREE or more techniques from requirement 3(c): (1) Drawstring backpack (2) Camp utensil holder (3) Storage bag for tent stakes or school supplies (4) Pillowcase (5) An item of your own choosing, approved in advance by your counselor. (B) Knitting (a) Provide a brief overview of the history of knitting. (b) Explain the tools used when knitting. Demonstrate the ability to read a pattern, including deciphering symbols. (c) Using knitting needles, demonstrate how to tie a slip knot, cast on and bind off. (d) Demonstrate the following stitches: (1) Knit stitch (2) Purl stitch. (e) Knit a small item such as a dishcloth, scarf, or an item of your own choosing, approved in advance by your counselor, using ONE of the following stitch patterns with at least two colors of yarn: (1) Garter stitch (2) Stockinette stitch (3) Ribbing. (C) Crochet (a) Provide a brief overview of the history of crochet OR the history of Amigurumi. (b) Explain the tools used when crocheting. Demonstrate the ability to read a pattern, including deciphering symbols. (c) Demonstrate how to tie a slip knot and how to hold a crochet hook and yarn to crochet. (d) Demonstrate the following stitches in a small practice piece: (1) Single crochet (2) Double crochet (3) Half-double crochet. (e) Crochet a small item such as a dishcloth, scrub, or an item of your own choosing, approved in advance by your counselor, using at least two colors of yarn. (D) Hand Embroidery (a) Provide a brief overview of the history of hand embroidery. (b) Explain the tools used in hand embroidery. (c) Embroider a small sampler of your own design or from a purchased kit or embroider a temporary patch for your uniform. Include SIX of the following basic stitches: running stitch, back stitch, stem stitch, chain stitch, surface couching, blanket stitch, herringbone stitch, chevron stitch, feather stitch, weave stitch, seed stitch, French knots, fishbone stitch, satin stitch, cross stitch. (E) Appliqué (a) Provide a brief overview of the history of hand appliqué. (b) In a small sample, demonstrate how to do appliqué by hand using the following methods: needle turn or freezer paper using an invisible (ladder) stitch or blanket stitch. (c) (c) In a small sample, demonstrate machine appliqué using a raw edge fusible technique and a blanket stitch. (d) Appliqué a design onto a T-shirt by hand or machine or reverse appliqué a shape by hand sewing. (F) Quilting (a) Research historical quilts and show your counselor examples of types of quilts that interest you. Discuss how they were made. (b) Explain the tools used when quilting and how to use them safely. Discuss why accuracy is important in traditional quilting. Sew an accurate ¼" seam. (c) Using scraps of cotton quilting fabric, sort into light, medium and dark colors. Choose a focus fabric and find a group of fabrics that would work well in a scrap quilt. Demonstrate how the value and scale of a printed fabric can create interest. (d) Using three copies of a quilting design, color blocks to achieve different quilt designs. Show your counselor your designs and which one is your favorite. (e) Make a small quilt (12" square plus borders): (1) Using a rotary cutter, cut fabric into strips and pieces to make a four patch, rail fence block pattern, or design of your choice. Sew together on a machine or by hand using a ¼" seam allowance and press flat. Cut and add borders. (2) Make a sandwich with backing and batting. Baste. (3) Hand quilt with a running stitch or big stitch. (4) Label your quilt. Explain why this is important. (5) Bind to finish the edge of the quilt.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which pair of sewing machine components works together to move the fabric forward by one stitch length after each needle penetration?
quiz_item.question: Which pair of sewing machine components works together to move the fabric forward by one stitch length after each needle penetration?
options: A. The bobbin winder spindle and the upper thread spool pin
B. The tension dial and the thread take-up lever
C. The feed dogs beneath the needle plate and the presser foot above
D. The flywheel clutch and the reverse stitch button
choices: A. The bobbin winder spindle and the upper thread spool pin
B. The tension dial and the thread take-up lever
C. The feed dogs beneath the needle plate and the presser foot above
D. The flywheel clutch and the reverse stitch button
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The feed dogs beneath the needle plate and the presser foot above
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The toothed feed dogs rise through slots in the throat plate to grip the underside of the fabric against the downward pressure of the presser foot, advancing the material evenly between stitches (p. 16).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When examining a traditional quilt at a textile exhibition, what are the three distinct layers held together by the quilting stitches?
quiz_item.question: When examining a traditional quilt at a textile exhibition, what are the three distinct layers held together by the quilting stitches?
options: A. The warp threads, the weft threads, and the selvedge edge
B. The paper pattern, the fusible interfacing, and the outer canvas lining
C. The embroidery hoop, the monk's cloth foundation, and the yarn fringe
D. The decorative pieced top, the insulating middle batting, and the fabric backing
choices: A. The warp threads, the weft threads, and the selvedge edge
B. The paper pattern, the fusible interfacing, and the outer canvas lining
C. The embroidery hoop, the monk's cloth foundation, and the yarn fringe
D. The decorative pieced top, the insulating middle batting, and the fabric backing
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. The decorative pieced top, the insulating middle batting, and the fabric backing
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A quilt sandwich consists of three layers: the decorative top (often pieced or appliqued), the warm inner batting, and the bottom backing fabric, all joined by hand or machine quilting stitches (p. 23).

requirements.req_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Identify three career opportunities that would use skills and knowledge in sewing and/or needlework. Pick one and research the training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (b) Identify how you might use the skills and knowledge in sewing and/or needlework to pursue a personal hobby. Research the additional training required, expenses, and affiliation with organizations that would help you maximize the enjoyment and benefit you might gain from it. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and share what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: While sewing a heavy canvas Merit Badge sash repair on a sewing machine, the needle hits a thick seam and snaps. What is the mandatory safety and machine procedure before replacing the needle?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: While sewing a heavy canvas Merit Badge sash repair on a sewing machine, the needle hits a thick seam and snaps. What is the mandatory safety and machine procedure before replacing the needle?
options: A. Keep your foot on the presser-foot speed controller while reaching into the needle bar.

B. Turn off and unplug the sewing machine first, locate all broken needle fragments so none remain in the fabric, and insert a fresh heavy-duty needle with the flat shank side facing the correct direction.
C. Leave the broken needle tip inside the canvas and sew over it.
D. Hold the replacement needle between your lips while loosening the needle clamp screw with power on.
choices: A. Keep your foot on the presser-foot speed controller while reaching into the needle bar.

B. Turn off and unplug the sewing machine first, locate all broken needle fragments so none remain in the fabric, and insert a fresh heavy-duty needle with the flat shank side facing the correct direction.
C. Leave the broken needle tip inside the canvas and sew over it.
D. Hold the replacement needle between your lips while loosening the needle clamp screw with power on.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Turn off and unplug the sewing machine first, locate all broken needle fragments so none remain in the fabric, and insert a fresh heavy-duty needle with the flat shank side facing the correct direction.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Turning off power prevents accidental foot-pedal activation while fingers are near the needle bar, and recovering broken needle tips prevents puncture injuries.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When hand sewing a flat button onto a shirt or jacket, why do tailors place a toothpick or pin across the top of the button while stitching?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When hand sewing a flat button onto a shirt or jacket, why do tailors place a toothpick or pin across the top of the button while stitching?
options: A. To keep the needle from dulling against the plastic rim of the button
B. To create slack for wrapping a thread shank underneath the button
C. To measure the exact distance between the buttonholes on the placket
D. To lock the quilter's knot on the front side of the garment
choices: A. To keep the needle from dulling against the plastic rim of the button
B. To create slack for wrapping a thread shank underneath the button
C. To measure the exact distance between the buttonholes on the placket
D. To lock the quilter's knot on the front side of the garment
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. To create slack for wrapping a thread shank underneath the button
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Stitching over a pin or toothpick creates controlled slack that you wrap with thread beneath the button to form a sturdy shank, giving the buttonhole fabric space to sit flat when buttoned (p. 13).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which pair of sewing machine components works together to move the fabric forward by one stitch length after each needle penetration?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which pair of sewing machine components works together to move the fabric forward by one stitch length after each needle penetration?
options: A. The bobbin winder spindle and the upper thread spool pin
B. The tension dial and the thread take-up lever
C. The feed dogs beneath the needle plate and the presser foot above
D. The flywheel clutch and the reverse stitch button
choices: A. The bobbin winder spindle and the upper thread spool pin
B. The tension dial and the thread take-up lever
C. The feed dogs beneath the needle plate and the presser foot above
D. The flywheel clutch and the reverse stitch button
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The feed dogs beneath the needle plate and the presser foot above
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The toothed feed dogs rise through slots in the throat plate to grip the underside of the fabric against the downward pressure of the presser foot, advancing the material evenly between stitches (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When examining a traditional quilt at a textile exhibition, what are the three distinct layers held together by the quilting stitches?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When examining a traditional quilt at a textile exhibition, what are the three distinct layers held together by the quilting stitches?
options: A. The warp threads, the weft threads, and the selvedge edge
B. The paper pattern, the fusible interfacing, and the outer canvas lining
C. The embroidery hoop, the monk's cloth foundation, and the yarn fringe
D. The decorative pieced top, the insulating middle batting, and the fabric backing
choices: A. The warp threads, the weft threads, and the selvedge edge
B. The paper pattern, the fusible interfacing, and the outer canvas lining
C. The embroidery hoop, the monk's cloth foundation, and the yarn fringe
D. The decorative pieced top, the insulating middle batting, and the fabric backing
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. The decorative pieced top, the insulating middle batting, and the fabric backing
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A quilt sandwich consists of three layers: the decorative top (often pieced or appliqued), the warm inner batting, and the bottom backing fabric, all joined by hand or machine quilting stitches (p. 23).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Before loading a 12-gauge shotgun on the range, why must you check the barrel for obstructions and verify that no smaller 20-gauge shell is mixed into your ammunition pouch?
quiz_item.question: Before loading a 12-gauge shotgun on the range, why must you check the barrel for obstructions and verify that no smaller 20-gauge shell is mixed into your ammunition pouch?
options: A. A 20-gauge shell has a wider brass rim that refuses to enter a 12-gauge receiver.
B. Mixing gauges causes the clay target thrower to release targets at the wrong angle.
C. A 20-gauge shell contains black powder that corrodes modern smokeless-powder chokes.
D. A 20-gauge shell dropped into a 12-gauge chamber will slide partway down the barrel and lodge out of sight; if a 12-gauge shell is then loaded and fired behind it, the barrel will burst.
choices: A. A 20-gauge shell has a wider brass rim that refuses to enter a 12-gauge receiver.
B. Mixing gauges causes the clay target thrower to release targets at the wrong angle.
C. A 20-gauge shell contains black powder that corrodes modern smokeless-powder chokes.
D. A 20-gauge shell dropped into a 12-gauge chamber will slide partway down the barrel and lodge out of sight; if a 12-gauge shell is then loaded and fired behind it, the barrel will burst.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. A 20-gauge shell dropped into a 12-gauge chamber will slide partway down the barrel and lodge out of sight; if a 12-gauge shell is then loaded and fired behind it, the barrel will burst.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A 20-gauge shell is narrow enough to slip past a 12-gauge chamber and lodge in the forcing cone, creating a catastrophic '12/20 burst' obstruction if a 12-gauge shell is chambered and fired behind it.

requirements.req_text: Working under the supervision of a certified National Rifle Association (NRA) Shotgun instructor and a certified range safety officer, at a nationally authorized camp property or at a commercial firearm range (as defined in the Scouting America National Range and Target Activities Manual ), do ONE of the following options: (a) Option A, Shotgun Shooting (Modern Shotshell Type). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify and explain the principal parts of a shotgun, action types, and how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a shotgun. (3) Identify the parts of a shotgun shell and their functions. (4) Identify the various gauges of shotguns. Explain which you would choose for a particular use and why. (5) Identify the causes of a shotgun's failure to fire, and explain what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are. sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option A, Shotgun Shooting (Modern Shotshell Type). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify and explain the principal parts of a shotgun, action types, and how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a shotgun. (3) Identify the parts of a shotgun shell and their functions. (4) Identify the various gauges of shotguns. Explain which you would choose for a particular use and why. (5) Identify the causes of a shotgun's failure to fire, and explain what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are. Explain and demonstrate proper preventive measures, and the procedures to follow in response to each. (6) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a shotgun on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (7) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a shotgun, and identify the materials needed. (8) Demonstrate how to clean a shotgun properly and safely. (9) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a shotgun. (10) Shoot a moving target with a shotgun using the four fundamentals of firing a shot, position, mount, vision, and movement. Shooting score required: Hit at least 12 out of 25 targets (48%) in two 25-target groups. The two groups need not be shot in consecutive order. A minimum of 50 shots must be fired. Shooting skill rules: Targets may be thrown by a hand trap, manual mechanical trap, or on any trap or skeet field. If using a hand trap or manual mechanical trap, the trap operator should be at least 5 feet to the right and 3 feet to the rear of the shooter. If throwing left-handed with a hand trap, the trap operator should be at least 5 feet to the left and 3 feet to the rear of the shooter. All targets should be thrown at a reasonable speed and in the same direction. Targets should be generally thrown so as to climb in the air after leaving the trap. Scores may be fired at any time, either in formal competition or in practice, but only under approved supervision and at an approved range as noted in the Scouting America National Range and Target Activities Manual. Modern, age-appropriate, target shotgun models, 12-, 16-, or 20-gauge, may be used. Only commercially manufactured ammunition may be used. Reloads may not be used in Scouting America range and target activities. Shooters must shoot in rounds of 25. Rounds need not be shot continuously or on the same day. The term "round" refers to a single series of 25 shots. If using a trap field, shoot station 3 with traps set to throw straightaway targets. If using a skeet field, shoot station 7 low house.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Modern Shotshell Shotgun Shooting: Sinceit is a close-range sport, guns with skeet or improved cylinderchokes using No. 8 or No. 9 shot are preferred (p. 47).
pamphlet_excerpts: Modern Shotshell Shotgun Shooting: Sinceit is a close-range sport, guns with skeet or improved cylinderchokes using No. 8 or No. 9 shot are preferred (p. 47).

sub_requirements.text: Option B, Muzzleloading Shotgun Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Discuss with your counselor a brief history of the development of the muzzleloading shotgun. (2) Identify principal parts of muzzleloading shotguns and discuss how they function. (3) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a muzzleloading shotgun. (4) Identify the various grades of black powder and explain their proper and safe use. (5) Discuss proper safety procedures pertaining to black powder storage. (6) Discuss proper components of a load. (7) Identify proper procedures and accessories used for safely loading a muzzleloading shotgun. (8) Identify the causes of a muzzleloading shotgun's failure to fire, and explain what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are. Explain and demonstrate proper preventive measures, and the procedures to follow in response to each. (9) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a muzzleloading shotgun on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (10) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a muzzleloading shotgun, and identify the materials needed. (11) Demonstrate how to clean a muzzleloading shotgun properly and safely. (12) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a muzzleloading shotgun. (13) Shoot a moving target with a muzzleloading shotgun using the four fundamentals of firing a shot, position, mount, vision, and movement. Shooting score required: Hit at least 5 out of 15 targets in each of two 15-target groups. The two groups need not be shot in consecutive order. A minimum of 30 shots must be fired. Shooting skill rules: Targets may be thrown by a hand trap, manual mechanical trap, or on any trap or skeet field. If using a hand trap or manual mechanical trap, the trap operator should be at least 5 feet to the right and 3 feet to the rear of the shooter. If throwing left-handed with a hand trap, the trap operator should be at least 5 feet to the left and 3 feet to the rear of the shooter. All targets should be thrown at a reasonable speed and in the same direction. Targets should be generally thrown so as to climb in the air after leaving the trap. Scores may be fired at any time, either in formal competition or in practice, but only under approved supervision and at an approved range as noted in the Scouting America National Range and Target Activities Manual. A 10 gauge or smaller muzzleloading rifle in appropriate size for the participant may be used. Matchlock, wheellock, or flintlock firearms are not approved. Standard clay targets customarily used for trap and skeet are to be used. On a standard trap field, the shooter should be positioned 8 yards behind the trap house. The trap should be set to throw only straightaway targets. If using a skeet field, shoot station 7 low house.

children.sub_req_text: Shoot a moving target with a muzzleloading shotgun using the four fundamentals of firing a shot, position, mount, vision, and movement. Shooting score required: Hit at least 5 out of 15 targets in each of two 15-target groups. The two groups need not be shot in consecutive order. A minimum of 30 shots must be fired. Shooting skill rules: Targets may be thrown by a hand trap, manual mechanical trap, or on any trap or skeet field. If using a hand trap or manual mechanical trap, the trap operator should be at least 5 feet to the right and 3 feet to the rear of the shooter. If throwing left-handed with a hand trap, the trap operator should be at least 5 feet to the left and 3 feet to the rear of the shooter. All targets should be thrown at a reasonable speed and in the same direction. Targets should be generally thrown so as to climb in the air after leaving the trap. Scores may be fired at any time, either in formal competition or in practice, but only under approved supervision and at an approved range as noted in the Scouting America National Range and Target Activities Manual. A 10 gauge or smaller muzzleloading rifle in appropriate size for the participant may be used. Matchlock, wheellock, or flintlock firearms are not approved. Standard clay targets customarily used for trap and skeet are to be used. On a standard trap field, the shooter should be positioned 8 yards behind the trap house. The trap should be set to throw only straightaway targets. If using a skeet field, shoot station 7 low house.

(10) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a muzzleloading shotgun, and identify the materials needed. (11) Demonstrate how to clean a muzzleloading shotgun properly and safely. quiz_item.question: In standard skeet shooting, why do shooters typically prefer a skeet or improved cylinder choke paired with No. 8 or No. 9 shot?
options: A. Because tighter full chokes are illegal in all National Skeet Shooting Association events
B. Because larger buckshot pellets travel too slowly to reach the high house trap
C. Because No. 9 shot contains more brass in the hull to prevent misfires
D. Because skeet targets are engaged at close range and benefit from a wider, dense pattern of small pellets
choices: A. Because tighter full chokes are illegal in all National Skeet Shooting Association events
B. Because larger buckshot pellets travel too slowly to reach the high house trap
C. Because No. 9 shot contains more brass in the hull to prevent misfires
D. Because skeet targets are engaged at close range and benefit from a wider, dense pattern of small pellets
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Because skeet targets are engaged at close range and benefit from a wider, dense pattern of small pellets
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Because skeet is a close-range clay target sport, open chokes like skeet or improved cylinder combined with small No. 8 or No. 9 pellets produce an even, wide pattern ideal for breaking targets at roughly 21 yards (p. 47).

B. Mixing gauges causes the clay target thrower to release targets at the wrong angle.

choices: A. A 20-gauge shell has a wider brass rim that refuses to enter a 12-gauge receiver.

common_misconception_pair.misconception: Many Scouts assume that signs, signals, and codes are interchangeable terms for any nonverbal gesture.
common_misconception_pair.fact: A sign is a static visual marker representing an object or direction, a signal is a dynamic action that transmits a live message across a distance, and a code is a structured system of rules for converting letters or words into another form (p. 7).
common_misconception_pair.fact_correction: A sign is a static visual marker representing an object or direction, a signal is a dynamic action that transmits a live message across a distance, and a code is a structured system of rules for converting letters or words into another form (p. 7).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the universal international distress call in Morse code, and what pattern of audible or visual signals is recognized worldwide as an emergency call for help?
quiz_item.question: What is the universal international distress call in Morse code, and what pattern of audible or visual signals is recognized worldwide as an emergency call for help?
options: A. Four short flashes followed by two long whistle blasts, repeated once every hour.
B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
C. A single continuous horn blast lasting ten seconds or waving a green flag overhead.
D. Two short whistle blasts repeated every thirty seconds, which means all clear in wilderness navigation.
choices: A. Four short flashes followed by two long whistle blasts, repeated once every hour.
B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
C. A single continuous horn blast lasting ten seconds or waving a green flag overhead.
D. Two short whistle blasts repeated every thirty seconds, which means all clear in wilderness navigation.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Three of anything (three whistle blasts, three fires or smoke columns, three light flashes) and Morse code SOS (three dots, three dashes, three dots) are universally recognized emergency distress signals.

options: A. The party has found safe shelter and requires no assistance
B. The group is moving north toward the nearest paved road
C. The survivors on the ground require general search-and-rescue assistance
D. A helicopter can safely land directly on top of the marked spot
choices: A. The party has found safe shelter and requires no assistance
B. The group is moving north toward the nearest paved road
C. The survivors on the ground require general search-and-rescue assistance

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The survivors on the ground require general search-and-rescue assistance
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): In international ground-to-air emergency signaling, a large V constructed on open ground means "Require assistance," while an X means "Require medical assistance" (p. 8).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How is a dash timed relative to a dot when transmitting a clear message in international Morse code?
quiz_item.question: How is a dash timed relative to a dot when transmitting a clear message in international Morse code?
options: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
B. Twice the duration of a single dot, with no pause needed between individual letters
C. Five times the duration of a single dot, sent only over electrical telegraph wires
D. Equal in length to a dot, distinguished only by using a higher audio pitch
choices: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
B. Twice the duration of a single dot, with no pause needed between individual letters
C. Five times the duration of a single dot, sent only over electrical telegraph wires
D. Equal in length to a dot, distinguished only by using a higher audio pitch
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In international Morse code timing, a dash is three times as long as a dot, the pause between letters is three dot-lengths, and the pause between words is seven dot-lengths (p. 6).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Because semaphore uses the same arm angles for the letters A through J as it does for the digits 1 through 0, how does a sender indicate that numbers are being transmitted?
quiz_item.question: Because semaphore uses the same arm angles for the letters A through J as it does for the digits 1 through 0, how does a sender indicate that numbers are being transmitted?
options: A. Switch from red-and-yellow flags to blue-and-white flags before signaling numbers
B. Wave both flags in a continuous figure-eight above the head during each digit
C. Kneel on one knee so the receiver knows the clock positions represent digits
D. Send the dedicated "numerals" position first, then send the "letters" signal when returning to text
choices: A. Switch from red-and-yellow flags to blue-and-white flags before signaling numbers
B. Wave both flags in a continuous figure-eight above the head during each digit
C. Kneel on one knee so the receiver knows the clock positions represent digits
D. Send the dedicated "numerals" position first, then send the "letters" signal when returning to text
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Send the dedicated "numerals" position first, then send the "letters" signal when returning to text
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): In semaphore, letters and numbers share the same arm angles, so the sender must flash the "numerals" signal before sending digits and the "letters" (or "J") signal to return to text (p. 8).

quiz_item.question: How does standard six-dot Braille distinguish a capital letter from a lowercase letter?
options: A. By embossing the raised dots twice as large as standard lowercase dots
B. By placing a special capital-indicator cell (dot 6) immediately before the letter
C. By inverting the six-dot cell upside down for every uppercase character
D. By using an eight-dot cell for capitals and a four-dot cell for lowercase letters
choices: A. By embossing the raised dots twice as large as standard lowercase dots
B. By placing a special capital-indicator cell (dot 6) immediately before the letter
C. By inverting the six-dot cell upside down for every uppercase character
D. By using an eight-dot cell for capitals and a four-dot cell for lowercase letters
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. By placing a special capital-indicator cell (dot 6) immediately before the letter
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In Braille, capital letters use the same cell patterns as lowercase letters but are preceded by a special cell with a single dot in position 6 (the capital indicator) (p. 6).

options: A. Raise the load slowly while swinging the boom to the operator's left
B. Lower the boom while holding the load height constant
C. Shut down the engine and secure the cab for the end of the shift
D. Execute an immediate Emergency Stop of all equipment movement

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: On a standard topographical map, what do symbols and lines printed in brown ink represent?
quiz_item.question: On a standard topographical map, what do symbols and lines printed in brown ink represent?
options: A. Unpaved backcountry dirt roads and seasonal four-wheel-drive tracks
B. Contour lines and relief features showing terrain elevation and shape
C. Dense woodland canopy, national forest boundaries, and scrub brush
D. Intermittent desert streams, dry washes, and seasonal marshlands
choices: A. Unpaved backcountry dirt roads and seasonal four-wheel-drive tracks
B. Contour lines and relief features showing terrain elevation and shape
C. Dense woodland canopy, national forest boundaries, and scrub brush
D. Intermittent desert streams, dry washes, and seasonal marshlands
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Contour lines and relief features showing terrain elevation and shape
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): On standard U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) topographical maps, brown is used for contour lines representing terrain elevation and relief features, while blue represents water and green represents vegetation (p. 9).

C. Writing the message in rows inside a grid and reading the letters out column by column
D. Looking up whole words in a two-part codebook and replacing each word with a five-digit number
choices: A. Replacing every letter in the message with the letter three places ahead in the alphabet
B. Swapping each letter for a tic-tac-toe grid shape containing a dot in the Pigpen cipher
C. Writing the message in rows inside a grid and reading the letters out column by column
D. Looking up whole words in a two-part codebook and replacing each word with a five-digit number
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Writing the message in rows inside a grid and reading the letters out column by column
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A transposition cipher (such as a rail fence or columnar cipher) keeps the original plaintext letters intact but scrambles their positions according to a geometric pattern or key (p. 7).
